        "text": "- id: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  title: Run result fields\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"Every run shall end with a run record holding the fields below. Each field describes one\\\n    \\ thing only, and only the combinations in the validity table are allowed.\\n\\n| Field | Values | Set\\\n    \\ by | Present when |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `run_outcome` | `COMPLETED`, `INCOMPLETE` | Run engine\\\n    \\ | Always |\\n| `stop_reason` | `MODEL_FAILURE`, `DATA_FAILURE`, `BUDGET`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`,\\\n    \\ `INTERRUPTED` | Run engine | Only when `INCOMPLETE` |\\n| `rating` | Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight,\\\n    \\ Sell, `REVIEW` | Portfolio Manager, read by the rating parser | Only when `COMPLETED` |\\n| `output_check`\\\n    \\ | `PASSED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `NOT_RUN` | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always |\\n| `check_findings` |\\\n    \\ List of rule IDs, each marked blocking or corrected | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always (may be empty)\\\n    \\ |\\n| `data_coverage` | One code per channel (FR-005) | FR-005 | Always |\\n\\n**Stop reasons**:\\n\\n\\\n    | Reason | Kind | Raised when | Owner of the rule |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `MODEL_FAILURE` | Failure\\\n    \\ | A model step produced no usable output after retries and the free-text fallback; also an authentication\\\n    \\ or provider-configuration error (`runapi/finalize.py:classify_exception` maps `authentication` and\\\n    \\ any `openai`/`anthropic`/`google`/`langchain` exception here) | NFR-001 |\\n| `DATA_FAILURE` | Failure\\\n    \\ | Core data is unavailable, absent or stale | FR-005, FR-006 |\\n| `BUDGET` | Planned stop | A required\\\n    \\ model request is refused by the run budget. A workflow that finishes within budget completes normally;\\\n    \\ which limit was hit goes to the log (OBS-001), not to the status. | PERF-002, COST-001, COST-002\\\n    \\ |\\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Failure | A defect or unmapped exception in the system's own code. Never\\\n    \\ used for budget exhaustion. | none (the default for an unclassified exception) |\\n| `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`\\\n    \\ | Failure | Writing or committing the report or manifest failed before publication | NFR-REPRO-001\\\n    \\ |\\n| `INTERRUPTED` | Planned stop | The run was cooperatively cancelled. Not a claim of durability\\\n    \\ through power loss. | FR-003 (resume), D-5 |\\n\\n**Spelling rule** (B2, Member B, 2026-11-23). The\\\n    \\ two failure values keep the spellings the\\nimplementation already serializes: `MODEL_FAILURE` and\\\n    \\ `DATA_FAILURE`. The draft's short forms\\n`MODEL` and `DATA` are human-facing labels only and are\\\n    \\ not values. Renaming a serialized value is a\\nbreaking change for existing evidence, validators\\\n    \\ and readers, so no requirement here asks for one.\\n`BUDGET` is the only addition; adding an enum\\\n    \\ value is not automatically supported by every existing\\nreader, so every reader must be updated\\\n    \\ or it will reject the new value.\\n\\n**Precedence rule** (B, 2026-11-23). Exactly one primary reason\\\n    \\ is recorded. If critical\\nreport-or-manifest publication fails, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is primary (NFR-REPRO-001,\\\n    \\ INV-14) and the\\ninitiating cause is retained in the safe diagnostic. A budget refusal is never\\\n    \\ reported as\\n`INTERNAL_ERROR`; if a budget stop and a persistence failure occur together, the persistence\\\n    \\ failure\\nis primary and the budget cause is recorded as secondary.\\n\\n**Mapping rule** (exactly\\\n    \\ one reason per run):\\n\\n1. These six values are the complete vocabulary. Every `INCOMPLETE` run\\\n    \\ shall map to exactly one of\\n   them, and a run that ends for an unlisted reason is a defect, not\\\n    \\ a new value.\\n2. Budget exhaustion shall be reported as `BUDGET`. It shall never be relabelled `INTERNAL_ERROR`\\\n    \\ or\\n   reported as a successful run.\\n3. A `BUDGET` or `INTERRUPTED` stop shall not be relabelled\\\n    \\ `MODEL_FAILURE` or `DATA_FAILURE`; those\\n   two describe a failure of the model or the data, not\\\n    \\ of a configured limit or a cancellation.\\n4. A budget refusal must be recognised before the generic\\\n    \\ exception classifier runs, and the memory\\n   settlement step and the structured-output fallback\\\n    \\ must not swallow it.\\n\\n**Validity table** (every other combination is invalid):\\n\\n| `run_outcome`\\\n    \\ | `stop_reason` | `rating` | `output_check` |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `INCOMPLETE` | any one of the\\\n    \\ six | — | `NOT_RUN` |\\n| `COMPLETED` | — | Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell | `PASSED`\\\n    \\ or `NEEDS_REVIEW` |\\n| `COMPLETED` | — | `REVIEW` | `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1) |\\n\\n**Evidence note.**\\\n    \\ No live attempt in `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` ends\\n`INCOMPLETE`: all\\\n    \\ 15 deduplicated attempts are `COMPLETED` with a null stop reason (verified\\n2026-11-23). Persistence\\\n    \\ and interruption behaviour is supported by the typed contract and offline\\nfault tests, not by that\\\n    \\ cohort.\"\n  fit_criterion: Given every offline fixture in Appendix A plus 6 one-per-reason fixtures, when each runs,\n    then (a) 100% of runs produce a run record; (b) 100% of records match exactly one row of the validity\n    table; (c) each of the 6 stop reasons appears at least once and 6/6 map to the reason declared for\n    their fixture; (d) 0 records have `COMPLETED` while some agent step produced no output; (e) 0 budget-exhaustion\n    fixtures are labelled `INTERNAL_ERROR`; (f) 0 records carry a reason outside the six-value vocabulary\n    (1 unlisted reason = 1 blocking defect).\n  tradeoff: The report header shows three short lines (outcome, rating, check) instead of one.\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against the team repository `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The result contract\n    now exists: `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` defines `RunOutcome = COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE`, a `StopReason`\n    literal, `OutputCheck = PASSED|NEEDS_REVIEW|NOT_RUN`, and `RunResult` with cross-field invariants\n    (COMPLETED needs a rating and no stop reason; INCOMPLETE needs no rating, a stop reason and NOT_RUN).\n    `runapi/execution.py` builds the envelope and `runapi/finalize.py` maps exceptions to stop reasons.\n    The raw graph entry `propagate` still returns `(final_state, signal)` where `signal` is a 5-tier rating\n    or `REVIEW` (`graph/trading_graph.py`, `agents/rating.py`). The gap is the vocabulary, not the contract:\n    the enum holds MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR and INTERRUPTED, and\n    has no BUDGET (OQ-6).'\n  open: Add the fields to the run record (NFR-REPRO-001) and set them on every exit path.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n  amended_by:\n  - D-3\n  - D-5\n  note: 'Decision OQ-6, resolved 2026-11-23 and revised the same day after Member B''s reply. The stop-reason\n    vocabulary is six values: `MODEL_FAILURE`, `DATA_FAILURE`, `BUDGET`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`,\n    `INTERRUPTED`. The first two keep the spellings the implementation already uses (`tradingagents/runapi/result.py:12-14`\n    at `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`); A had briefly required `MODEL`/`DATA` and accepted B''s objection (B2)\n    that renaming is a breaking change to a serialized public value consumed by 23 code/test sites and\n    9 documents, including C''s own STOP_REASONS set. `BUDGET` is the one addition and is not yet present\n    in the code; adding it is an implementation item for B/D (finalize, reporting, result validation,\n    regression fixtures), and every existing reader must be updated or it will reject the new value. The\n    other two values exist because a three-value table left `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and `INTERRUPTED` runs\n    without a valid row. B''s correction, accepted: no live evidence shows an `INCOMPLETE` attempt. All\n    15 deduplicated attempts in `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` are `COMPLETED`\n    with a null stop reason; persistence and interruption behaviour is supported by typed contracts and\n    offline tests, not by that live cohort. Non-normative, D-5: a resumed run keeps its `run_id` and adds\n    an attempt rather than starting a new run; the interrupted attempt is written `INCOMPLETE` and is\n    never edited afterwards; evaluation counts `run_id`s, not attempts. B notes that D-5 conflicts with\n    INV-11/INV-12''s fresh-run-ID and immutability rules and is therefore a separate contract change,\n    not implied by the vocabulary; it stays open (see requirement-source-notes.md OQ-8).'\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-001\n  title: Evidence IDs, records and visible source dates\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: 'The system shall give each evidence item admitted into a run one stable evidence ID, and\n    shall keep a record for it with at least: source, ticker, and either observation time or publication\n    time. Wherever the report cites an item, it shall show the item''s source and date (`YYYY-MM-DD`)\n    beside the citation. Records are kept for every run whatever its outcome: a run''s outcome never changes\n    or deletes its evidence records.'\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and `fixtures/fr001/evidence.jsonl`, when one run completes\n    and every cited ID is collected, then (a) 100% of cited IDs resolve to exactly 1 record with non-empty\n    `source`, `ticker` and one of `observed_at` / `published_at`; (b) 100% of citations in the rendered\n    report show a source and a date; (c) all 12 channels of FR-004 write records, including the 2 that\n    bypass the router. Given fixture `fixtures/fr001/timeout_after_price/`, which ends `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)`\n    after price data was retrieved, then (d) the registry still holds the price records, unchanged (≥\n    1 record, byte-identical to before the stop). An ID that is cited but not registered is the blocking\n    finding R2 (ARCH-002).\n  tradeoff: One write per admitted item and one lookup per citation, plus storage under `results_dir`.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  related: ARCH-001 (when it is met, the registry write can sit in the router alone)\n  baseline: Items carry their own dates and source labels in vendor text (news rows and price rows both\n    carry a date), but nothing assigns an ID or keeps a record keyed by one.\n  open: Add the registry write at the data boundary, including the two bypass channels, and render source\n    and date at each citation.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: tests/test_no_data_handling.py\n    locator: observed in v0.7.1\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-003\n  title: Checkpoint list, resume and rerun\n  type: functional\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: The system shall list saved checkpoints, resume an interrupted run without re-running tasks\n    that were already saved, and rerun from scratch on request.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and a run interrupted after all 4 analyst branches were saved,\n    when (a) it is resumed with the same ticker, *D* and settings, then agent invocations for those 4\n    branches = 0 (4/4); (b) the checkpoint list is shown, then it lists ticker, *D*, the run signature,\n    the number of saved tasks, and a status of `RESUMABLE` (signature matches current settings) or `CONFIG_CHANGED`\n    (it does not) — checked on 1 fixture of each status; (c) it is rerun, then all 4 branches execute\n    again (≥ 1 invocation each), the old checkpoint is cleared, and the rerun gets its own run record\n    and report per NFR-REPRO-001.\n  tradeoff: Checkpoints are stored per ticker, so the list is per ticker unless an index file is added.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: 'Resume already works: per-node SQLite checkpoints keyed by a run signature, resume detection\n    (`checkpoint_step`), fresh start when the signature changes, and clean-up after success (`graph/checkpointer.py`,\n    `_run_signature` in `trading_graph.py`; tests `test_checkpoint_resume.py`, `test_checkpoint_lifecycle.py`,\n    `test_graph_end_to_end.py::test_an_interrupted_run_resumes_from_its_checkpoint`). There is no list\n    command and no explicit rerun command.'\n  open: Add the list and rerun commands. Turn the three checks above into acceptance tests.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-003\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-004\n  title: Point-in-time evidence (no look-ahead)\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: For a run with analysis date *D*, no item published, observed, filed or resolved after the\n    end of *D* shall reach any agent's prompt, through any channel. A date the model gives a tool shall\n    never widen the window past *D*. Data with no historical version (live-only data) shall be withheld\n    from a run dated before today. The one exception is the instrument's current name, which may be given\n    only when it is labelled as the current name.\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile, *D* = 2026-01-09, and `fixtures/fr004/channels/` holding,\n    for each of the 10 dated channels, one control item dated *D* and one planted item dated *D*+1 that\n    carries the marker `LOOKAHEAD-<#>`, when one run executes and every prompt to the scripted model is\n    captured, then: (a) 0/10 markers appear in any prompt; (b) 10/10 control items appear in at least\n    one prompt; (c) the 2 live-only channels return their \"withheld\" notice (2/2) and 0 live values; (d)\n    for each of the 12 dated tools in `agents/tools.py`, a model-supplied date of *D*+30 is served as\n    *D* (12/12); (e) the instrument context holds 0 sector, industry or exchange values, and any name\n    carries the \"current name\" label.'\n  tradeoff: Historical runs see less data than a live run would.\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: Each channel already has its own guard and unit tests (`test_tool_date_enforcement.py`, `test_news_lookahead.py`,\n    `test_social_lookahead.py`, `test_fundamentals_lookahead.py`, `test_memory_pointintime.py`, `test_undated_tools_as_of.py`,\n    `test_statement_knowledge_time.py`); a future *D* is refused (`_validate_trade_date`). No test checks\n    all channels in one whole run.\n  open: Add the whole-run planted-marker test as a required CI check.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-004\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-005\n  title: Data gaps and the core-data rule\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: \"This requirement owns every rule about missing data.\\n1. **Core rule.** If core data has\\\n    \\ any code other than `OK`, the run ends `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`.\\n2. **Non-core rule.** A gap in any other\\\n    \\ channel does not stop the run.\\n3. **Disclosure.** Every report has a \\\"Data coverage\\\" section\\\n    \\ that lists each channel with exactly one code from the table below. The section is built from tool\\\n    \\ results and is never written by the model. A channel that no selected analyst requested is reported\\\n    \\ as `NOT_REQUESTED`; it is never reported as a gap. (f) the section is byte-identical when the scripted model''s prose is replaced with\n    different prose.'\n  tradeoff: Every report gains a section, including gaps that a reader may not care about.\n  semantic_part: whether the model's own prose avoids claiming an absence (\"no recent news\") for a channel\n    that has a gap is tested in the GOV-001 suite, because a scripted model cannot test it.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-FR-004\n  baseline: The data layer already tells these cases apart in tool text and tells the model not to invent\n    values (`dataflows/router.py`, `date_window.py`; Stale data\\\n    \\ is coded `STALE` (FR-005) and handled as the last column says.\\n\\n| Data type | Fresh when | Parameter\\\n    \\ (Appendix D) | If exceeded |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Price history | Latest bar is ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS`\\\n    \\ calendar days before *D* | `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` | Not used; core gap → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)` (FR-005)\\\n    \\ |\\n| Technical indicators | Follows price history | — | Follows price history |\\n| Financial statements\\\n    \\ | Latest statement was filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` days before *D* | `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` |\\\n    \\ Still shown with its filing date; coded `STALE`; run continues |\\n| Ticker news, global news, social\\\n    \\ posts | Item lies inside the requested window, clamped to *D* (FR-004) | `global_news_lookback_days`\\\n    \\ (v0.7.1 config) | Item left out. Only the Portfolio Manager's output is called the final rating, and only\\\n    \\ it fills `rating` in the run record.\\n3. **No ownership wording.** Prompts and reports shall not\\\n    \\ state or assume that the user holds the instrument. Analysts already run in parallel (`graph/setup.py`).\n579:   open: Measure first, then fix `RUN_TIME_CAP` from the measurement.\n580:   source:\n581:   - kind: team_document\n582:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n583:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n584:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001\n585:   - kind: baseline_observation\n586:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n587:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n588: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002\n589:   title: Time-budget handling\n590:   type: performance\n591:   priority: Should\n592:   status: proposed\n593:   statement: A run that crosses its time budget (default `RUN_TIME_CAP`) shall stop and end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`.\n594:     Calls already in flight may run for at most `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE` beyond the budget.\n595:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile with a slow scripted model and a 30 s test budget, when 10\n596:     runs execute, then 10/10 end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`, 10/10 return within 30 s + `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE`,\n597:     and 10/10 logs name the time limit.\n598:   tradeoff: Calls that ignore cancellation delay the return.\n599:   metric: time from the deadline/cancel signal to the terminal event; terminal outcome\n600:   threshold: <= CANCEL_ALLOWANCE (2 s) and exactly 1 terminal event naming the budget; workflow within\n601:     budget completes normally\n602:   verification: offline profile; fixture that crosses the deadline mid-step and fixture cancelled between\n603:     steps\n604:   dependencies:\n605:   - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n606:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n607:   baseline: No run-level timer.\n608:   open: Check the deadline at node boundaries and add the cancellation allowance.\n609:   source:\n610:   - kind: team_document\n611:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n612:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n613:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002\n614:   - kind: baseline_observation\n615:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n616:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n617: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n618:   title: Run token budget\n619:   type: cost\n620:   priority: Should\n621:   status: proposed\n622:   statement: A run shall use at most `TOKEN_BUDGET` tokens in total, counted from provider usage data.\n623:     A run that would exceed it ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. If a provider returns no usage data, the run\n624:     is not stopped; its record marks token usage as `UNKNOWN`.\n625:   fit_criterion: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then 20/20 have known\n626:     usage ≤ `TOKEN_BUDGET`, and the GOV-001 score over these runs is ≥ `QUALITY_THRESHOLD`. A run with\n627:     `UNKNOWN` usage counts as a failure of this criterion, not as zero cost.\n628:   tradeoff: A budget forces shorter prompts or debates, which the quality threshold partly forbids.\n629:   metric: tokens consumed per run against TOKEN_BUDGET\n630:   threshold: tokens_used <= TOKEN_BUDGET; a run that exhausts the budget ends INCOMPLETE with stop_reason\n631:     BUDGET\n632:   verification: offline profile with a scripted model reporting token counts; one within-budget and one\n633:     exhaustion fixture\n634:   dependencies:\n635:   - REQ-TA-GOV-001\n636:   - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n637:   baseline: '`max_tokens` caps each call (`default_config.py`). There is no run-level count.'\n638:   open: Add up usage per run; set `TOKEN_BUDGET` from measurement.\n639:   source:\n640:   - kind: team_document\n641:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n642:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n643:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n644:   - kind: baseline_observation\n645:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n646:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n647: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n648:   title: Run-wide LLM call cap\n649:   type: cost\n650:   priority: Must\n651:   status: proposed\n652:   statement: 'The system shall ensure that, per run, the number of model-request dispatch attempts never\n653:     exceeds the number of successful reservations and never exceeds `CALL_CAP`: `dispatch_attempts <=\n654:     successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`. A dispatch attempt is one model-generation request attempt issued\n655:     through the controlled application client boundary, including attempts that time out or fail, application\n656:     retries, structured-output re-requests, free-text fallback, and in-run memory reflection requests.\n657:     Every attempt shall be preceded by its own fresh single-use reservation from the run''s shared budget\n658:     controller; a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, cannot be reused, and a denied reservation\n659:     dispatches nothing. An attempt that has been issued consumes its slot even if it fails. A workflow\n660:     that finishes within its cap completes normally; a run stops `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` only when a required\n661:     further attempt is refused.'\n662:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and `CALL_CAP = 8`, when a run executes, then (a) every controlled\n663:     request attempt has a unique preceding successful reservation from the same run; audit records pair\n664:     one reservation with at most one attempt, including retries, fallback and memory calls; a denied reservation\n665:     dispatches nothing; (b) total controlled request attempts ≤ 8 across all branches and model tiers,\n666:     with SDK automatic retries disabled for this mode or every underlying attempt independently gated\n667:     and counted; (c) after 7 slots are consumed, 4 workers contend for the remaining slot using an injected\n668:     barrier against the real reservation component, and exactly 1 succeeds and 3 are denied (the winner's\n669:     identity need not be deterministic); (d) in a scripted workflow that requires one more attempt after\n670:     the cap is exhausted, that attempt is refused and the run returns `INCOMPLETE` with `stop_reason =\n671:     BUDGET`, no final rating and `output_check = NOT_RUN`, with audit metadata naming the configured cap\n672:     and the counts; a workflow that completes within its cap ends normally.\n673:   tradeoff: A small shared cap can starve parallel branches, and a strict single-use reservation means\n674:     a branch that loses the last slot stops the run rather than degrading. The stricter the bound, the\n675:     less tolerant the system is of a borderline cap; that is the price of a guarantee that can actually\n676:     be checked.\n677:   metric: model-request dispatch attempts per run, against successful reservations and CALL_CAP\n678:   threshold: dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP (test value 8); 0 attempts issued\n679:     without a reservation\n680:   verification: offline profile; one budget-controller fixture with an injected threading barrier for\n681:     the last-slot race; audit log pairing reservations with attempts; one exhaustion fixture and one within-cap\n682:     fixture\n683:   dependencies:\n684:   - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n685:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n686:   baseline: 'Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds`\n687:     (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.'\n688:   open: Add a shared run-scoped counter and a reservation that precedes dispatch.\n689:   note: 'Decision D-3, revised 2026-11-23 after Member B''s technical reply. Non-normative. Application\n690:     counting equals real provider calls only when every attempt the application issues is an attempt the\n691:     provider sees. In the inspected baseline, `llm_max_retries` is forwarded to the provider SDK (`tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py`),\n692:     and analysts fan out concurrently from `START` (`tradingagents/graph/setup.py`), so a counter around\n693:     high-level model invocations cannot by itself guarantee the bound. Member B''s recommended mechanism\n694:     is one shared run-scoped budget controller with SDK retries disabled, where each application retry\n695:     takes a fresh single-use reservation; that makes the strict `<= CALL_CAP` bound achievable. How it\n696:     is built remains a B design and D implementation decision (`decision-request-D3-cost002-2026-11-22.md`,\n697:     reply of 2026-11-22). Because a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, concurrent branches hold\n698:     their own reservations and no branch allowance is needed; the earlier `CALL_CAP + N_concurrent_branches`\n699:     form is withdrawn. This requirement does not guarantee the provider gateway''s internal retry count,\n700:     exact billable usage or monetary cost, and it does not claim the bound is implemented: the controller\n701:     does not exist in the baseline. If D cannot make (a)-(d) hold on every enabled client, A downgrades\n702:     COST-002 from Must to Should and restates it as detection-only, recorded in D-4.'\n703:   source:\n704:   - kind: team_document\n705:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n706:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n707:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n708:   - kind: team_decision\n709:     ref: req-final-scope-A-2026-11-22.md#3\n710:     locator: D-3\n711:   - kind: team_document\n712:     ref: reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md\n713:     locator: Member B technical reply; strict bound and single-use reservation adopted 2026-11-23\n714:   - kind: baseline_observation\n715:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n716:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n717: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n718:   title: Early debate convergence\n719:   type: cost\n720:   priority: Could\n721:   status: proposed\n722:   statement: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when\n723:     the participants' positions have converged.\n724:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures,\n725:     when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for\n726:     4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n727:   tradeoff: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n728:   metric: debate rounds executed when the debate has converged\n729:   threshold: converged debate stops before max_debate_rounds (rounds_executed < max_debate_rounds on the\n730:     converged fixture); 0 premature stops on the non-converged fixture\n731:   verification: offline profile; one converged and one non-converged scripted debate\n732:   dependencies:\n733:   - REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n734:   baseline: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n735:   open: Define the convergence signal.\n736:   source:\n737:   - kind: team_document\n738:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n739:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n740:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n741:   - kind: baseline_observation\n742:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n743:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n744: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n745:   title: Evaluation counting rules\n746:   type: quality_evaluation\n747:   priority: Should\n748:   status: proposed\n749:   statement: \"Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\\n1. **Completion\\\n750:     \\ rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\\n2.\\\n751:     \\ **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only,\\\n752:     \\ and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\\n3. `INCOMPLETE`\\\n753:     \\ runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\\n4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001).\\\n754:     \\ Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\\n5. **Acceptance population.** `N_EVAL` counts\\\n755:     \\ distinct semantic cases, never attempts; a repeated attempt is a repeatability comparison under\\\n756:     \\ rule 6 and is not counted twice. A changed case population is a versioned acceptance change, not\\\n757:     \\ a re-run, and results across two populations are not compared. The counting rules below define arithmetic\\\n758:     \\ only: the rubric, the critical items, the profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are required acceptance\\\n759:     \\ inputs owned by Members D and E, and no counting result is an acceptance result without them.\\n\\\n760:     6. **Comparison modes.** Two results may be compared in *repeatability* mode only if their run records\\\n761:     \\ match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001); any difference between them is measurement\\\n762:     \\ noise and is reported as such. A *controlled change* comparison is permitted when exactly one factor\\\n763:     \\ (prompt, model or budget) is declared as changed and every other recorded key matches; the output\\\n764:     \\ must name that factor and report `factor: before -> after`, with the completion rate and the `NEEDS_REVIEW`\\\n765:     \\ count beside both sides. A comparison that changes more than one factor, or that does not declare\\\n766:     \\ the factor, is refused.\"\n767:   fit_criterion: 'Given 10 fixed run records used as a counting fixture (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are\n768:     `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA_FAILURE`, 2 `MODEL_FAILURE`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation\n769:     script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n770:     = 2, and stop reasons `DATA_FAILURE` 1, `MODEL_FAILURE` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped; and\n771:     the output states that these 10 records are a counting fixture, not an acceptance run under `N_EVAL`.\n772:     Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash` and declare no changed factor, the script refuses to\n773:     compare them (1/1); given 2 records differing only in `prompt_hash` that declare `prompt` as the changed\n774:     factor, it reports exactly 1 controlled-change comparison naming `prompt` (1/1); given 2 records differing\n775:     in both `prompt_hash` and `model` with no declaration, it refuses (1/1); given 20 cases scored twice\n776:     under identical `config` and `prompt_hash`, then `N_EVAL` is reported as 20 cases and not 40 attempts,\n777:     and exactly 1 result is counted.'\n778:   tradeoff: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single\n779:     blended number. That is intended.\n780:   metric: agreement between reported evaluation numbers and a recomputation from the same run records\n781:   threshold: 100% of reported counts equal the recomputed values; 0 runs silently removed from the completion\n782:     denominator; 0 undeclared multi-factor comparisons accepted\n783:   verification: recompute every reported figure from the stored run records of a fixed evidence set\n784:   dependencies:\n785:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n786:   - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n787:   baseline: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n788:   open: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n789:   source:\n790:   - kind: team_document\n791:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n792:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n793:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n794:   - kind: review_finding\n795:     ref: requirements-v2-review-2026-11-12.md\n796:     locator: V2-10\n797:   - kind: baseline_observation\n798:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n799:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n800:   note: 'Amended 2026-11-23 on Member B''s question. B asked whether `N_EVAL` counts cases or attempts\n801:     and whether the existing five cases and two trials establish acceptance under `N_EVAL=20` with an\n802:     open threshold. B was right that they do not, and A found a second defect of A''s own: the parameter\n803:     appendix says `N_EVAL` = 20 cases, while this criterion originally exercised 10 records without saying\n804:     they were not acceptance. Rule 5 is new and says both things explicitly. A did **not** fix the remainder,\n805:     because the rubric, the critical items, the evaluation profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are owned by\n806:     D and E and two of them are still open parameters; writing them here would have made `GOV-001` look\n807:     decided when it is not. Not implemented: no evaluation script exists in the baseline.'\n808: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n809:   title: Prompt-injection resistance\n810:   type: security\n811:   priority: Must\n812:   status: proposed\n813:   statement: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage`\n814:     record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n815:   fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals\n816:     content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT\n817:     CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its\n818:     output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage`\n819:     equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal\n820:     the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.'\n821:   tradeoff: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n822:   metric: injected instructions that change the rating or the output check\n823:   threshold: 0/20 injection fixtures change the final rating or the output_check; 20/20 still produce\n824:     a valid run record\n825:   verification: offline profile; injected text in every retrieved-text channel (news, social, filings,\n826:     web)\n827:   semantic_part: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n828:   dependencies:\n829:   - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n830:   - REQ-TA-FR-005\n831:   baseline: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified.\n832:     No deterministic check exists yet.\n833:   open: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n834:   source:\n835:   - kind: team_document\n836:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n837:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n838:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n839:   - kind: baseline_observation\n840:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n841:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n842: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n843:   title: No credential or token leakage\n844:   type: security\n845:   priority: Must\n846:   status: partial\n847:   statement: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens,\n848:     refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n849:   fit_criterion: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor\n850:     error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions\n851:     finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n852:   tradeoff: Less debugging detail in error text.\n853:   metric: secret occurrences in report, log, event stream and traceback on error paths\n854:   threshold: 0 occurrences of any planted secret in any sink; source files unmodified\n855:   verification: plant 4 secret types across every sink and every error path, then scan the captured output\n856:   dependencies: []\n857:   baseline: Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`)\n858:     redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by the Alpha Vantage and FRED vendor modules. The boundary\n859:     adds `runapi/redact.py`, a `Redactor` applied at the event, report and error sinks. Coverage of third-party\n860:     loggers and uncaught tracebacks outside the boundary remains unverified.\n861:   open: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n862:   source:\n863:   - kind: team_document\n864:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n865:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n866:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n867:   - kind: baseline_observation\n868:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n869:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n870: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n871:   title: No promise of guaranteed returns\n872:   type: security\n873:   priority: Should\n874:   status: proposed\n875:   statement: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed\n876:     profit or capital protection.\n877:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the\n878:     disclaimer string; (b) 5 scripted final decisions that each contain a phrase from `fixtures/sec003/guarantee_phrases.txt`\n879:     are checked, then 5/5 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R8.\n880:   tradeoff: The phrase list flags \"guaranteed\" even inside a quoted source.\n881:   metric: reports starting with the disclaimer, and guarantee phrases caught by rule R8\n882:   threshold: 20/20 reports start with the disclaimer; 5/5 guarantee fixtures get NEEDS_REVIEW with finding\n883:     R8\n884:   verification: offline profile; 20 rendered reports and 5 scripted decisions containing listed phrases\n885:   semantic_part: 5 live prompts that directly ask for a guarantee are in the GOV-001 suite.\n886:   dependencies:\n887:   - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n888:   baseline: The disclaimer exists in the README only.\n889:   open: Add the report disclaimer and rule R8.\n890:   source:\n891:   - kind: team_document\n892:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n893:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n894:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n895:   - kind: baseline_observation\n896:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n897:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n898: - id: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n899:   title: Vendors behind one routing point\n900:   type: architectural_constraint\n901:   priority: Should\n902:   status: partial\n903:   statement: Vendor access shall go through the router's method map, so agent and graph modules name a\n904:     method, never a vendor module or vendor SDK.\n905:   fit_criterion: Given `tradingagents/agents/**` and `tradingagents/graph/**`, when the import-boundary\n906:     test runs, then they import 0 times from `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.*` and 0 times from `yfinance`\n907:     (the only vendor SDK in `pyproject.toml`); and a fake vendor in the method map serves every evidence\n908:     request in the end-to-end test with 0 monkeypatches of agent modules.\n909:   tradeoff: One more indirection per call.\n910:   metric: direct vendor imports in agent modules\n911:   threshold: 0 direct vendor imports in `tradingagents/agents/**`; the layering test covers every vendor\n912:     package, not only `yfinance`\n913:   verification: static import scan anchored on the package boundary, enforced by `tests/test_layering.py`\n914:   dependencies: []\n915:   baseline: 'Not met. There are 4 direct vendor imports in 3 agent files: `agents/context.py` (Yahoo profile),\n916:     `agents/tools.py` (Yahoo snapshot) and `agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py` (Reddit, StockTwits).\n917:     `tests/test_layering.py` bans only the `yfinance` library.'\n918:   open: Move the 4 imports behind router methods and extend the layering test.\n919:   source:\n920:   - kind: team_document\n921:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n922:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n923:     locator: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n924:   - kind: baseline_observation\n925:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n926:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n927: - id: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n928:   title: Deterministic output check\n929:   type: architectural_constraint\n930:   priority: Must\n931:   status: proposed\n932:   statement: \"Exactly one deterministic, non-LLM component shall set `output_check` and `check_findings`.\\\n933:     \\ It runs on every `COMPLETED` run after the Portfolio Manager and applies the rules below. terminal outcome\n  threshold: <= CANCEL_ALLOWANCE (2 s) and exactly 1 terminal event naming the budget; workflow within\n    budget completes normally\n  verification: offline profile; fixture that crosses the deadline mid-step and fixture cancelled between\n    steps\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: No run-level timer.\n  open: Check the deadline at node boundaries and add the cancellation allowance.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n  title: Run token budget\n  type: cost\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: A run shall use at most `TOKEN_BUDGET` tokens in total, counted from provider usage data.\n    A run that would exceed it ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. A dispatch attempt is one model-generation request attempt issued\n    through the controlled application client boundary, including attempts that time out or fail, application\n    retries, structured-output re-requests, free-text fallback, and in-run memory reflection requests.\n    Every attempt shall be preceded by its own fresh single-use reservation from the run''s shared budget\n    controller; a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, cannot be reused, and a denied reservation\n    dispatches nothing. The stricter the bound, the\n    less tolerant the system is of a borderline cap; that is the price of a guarantee that can actually\n    be checked.\n  metric: model-request dispatch attempts per run, against successful reservations and CALL_CAP\n  threshold: dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP (test value 8); 0 attempts issued\n    without a reservation\n  verification: offline profile; one budget-controller fixture with an injected threading barrier for\n    the last-slot race; audit log pairing reservations with attempts; one exhaustion fixture and one within-cap\n    fixture\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: 'Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds`\n    (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.'\n  open: Add a shared run-scoped counter and a reservation that precedes dispatch.\n  note: 'Decision D-3, revised 2026-11-23 after Member B''s technical reply. Non-normative. Application\n    counting equals real provider calls only when every attempt the application issues is an attempt the\n    provider sees. In the inspected baseline, `llm_max_retries` is forwarded to the provider SDK (`tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py`),\n    and analysts fan out concurrently from `START` (`tradingagents/graph/setup.py`), so a counter around\n    high-level model invocations cannot by itself guarantee the bound. Member B''s recommended mechanism\n    is one shared run-scoped budget controller with SDK retries disabled, where each application retry\n    takes a fresh single-use reservation; that makes the strict `<= CALL_CAP` bound achievable. How it\n    is built remains a B design and D implementation decision (`decision-request-D3-cost002-2026-11-22.md`,\n    reply of 2026-11-22). Because a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, concurrent branches hold\n    their own reservations and no branch allowance is needed; the earlier `CALL_CAP + N_concurrent_branches`\n    form is withdrawn. This requirement does not guarantee the provider gateway''s internal retry count,\n    exact billable usage or monetary cost, and it does not claim the bound is implemented: the controller\n    does not exist in the baseline. If D cannot make (a)-(d) hold on every enabled client, A downgrades\n    COST-002 from Must to Should and restates it as detection-only, recorded in D-4.'\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n  - kind: team_decision\n    ref: req-final-scope-A-2026-11-22.md#3\n    locator: D-3\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md\n    locator: Member B technical reply; strict bound and single-use reservation adopted 2026-11-23\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n  title: Early debate convergence\n  type: cost\n  priority: Could\n  status: proposed\n  statement: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when\n    the participants' positions have converged.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures,\n    when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for\n    4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n  tradeoff: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n  metric: debate rounds executed when the debate has converged\n  threshold: converged debate stops before max_debate_rounds (rounds_executed < max_debate_rounds on the\n    converged fixture); 0 premature stops on the non-converged fixture\n  verification: offline profile; one converged and one non-converged scripted debate\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n  baseline: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n  open: Define the convergence signal.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n  title: Evaluation counting rules\n  type: quality_evaluation\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\\n1. **Completion\\\n    \\ rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\\n2.\\\n    \\ **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only,\\\n    \\ and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\\n3. `INCOMPLETE`\\\n    \\ runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\\n4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001).\\\n    \\ Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\\n5. **Acceptance population.** `N_EVAL` counts\\\n    \\ distinct semantic cases, never attempts; a repeated attempt is a repeatability comparison under\\\n    \\ rule 6 and is not counted twice. A changed case population is a versioned acceptance change, not\\\n    \\ a re-run, and results across two populations are not compared. The counting rules below define arithmetic\\\n    \\ only: the rubric, the critical items, the profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are required acceptance\\\n    \\ inputs owned by Members D and E, and no counting result is an acceptance result without them.\\n\\\n    6. **Comparison modes.** Two results may be compared in *repeatability* mode only if their run records\\\n    \\ match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001); any difference between them is measurement\\\n    \\ noise and is reported as such. A *controlled change* comparison is permitted when exactly one factor\\\n    \\ (prompt, model or budget) is declared as changed and every other recorded key matches; the output\\\n    \\ must name that factor and report `factor: before -> after`, with the completion rate and the `NEEDS_REVIEW`\\\n    \\ count beside both sides. A comparison that changes more than one factor, or that does not declare\\\n    \\ the factor, is refused.\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given 10 fixed run records used as a counting fixture (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are\n    `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA_FAILURE`, 2 `MODEL_FAILURE`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation\n    script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n    = 2, and stop reasons `DATA_FAILURE` 1, `MODEL_FAILURE` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped; and\n    the output states that these 10 records are a counting fixture, not an acceptance run under `N_EVAL`.\n    Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash` and declare no changed factor, the script refuses to\n    compare them (1/1); given 2 records differing only in `prompt_hash` that declare `prompt` as the changed\n    factor, it reports exactly 1 controlled-change comparison naming `prompt` (1/1); given 2 records differing\n    in both `prompt_hash` and `model` with no declaration, it refuses (1/1); given 20 cases scored twice\n    under identical `config` and `prompt_hash`, then `N_EVAL` is reported as 20 cases and not 40 attempts,\n    and exactly 1 result is counted.'\n  tradeoff: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single\n    blended number. That is intended.\n  metric: agreement between reported evaluation numbers and a recomputation from the same run records\n  threshold: 100% of reported counts equal the recomputed values; 0 runs silently removed from the completion\n    denominator; 0 undeclared multi-factor comparisons accepted\n  verification: recompute every reported figure from the stored run records of a fixed evidence set\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n  open: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n  - kind: review_finding\n    ref: requirements-v2-review-2026-11-12.md\n    locator: V2-10\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n  note: 'Amended 2026-11-23 on Member B''s question. B asked whether `N_EVAL` counts cases or attempts\n    and whether the existing five cases and two trials establish acceptance under `N_EVAL=20` with an\n    open threshold. B was right that they do not, and A found a second defect of A''s own: the parameter\n    appendix says `N_EVAL` = 20 cases, while this criterion originally exercised 10 records without saying\n    they were not acceptance. Rule 5 is new and says both things explicitly. A did **not** fix the remainder,\n    because the rubric, the critical items, the evaluation profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are owned by\n    D and E and two of them are still open parameters; writing them here would have made `GOV-001` look\n    decided when it is not. Not implemented: no evaluation script exists in the baseline.'\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n  title: Prompt-injection resistance\n  type: security\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage`\n    record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals\n    content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT\n    CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its\n    output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage`\n    equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal\n    the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.'\n  tradeoff: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n  metric: injected instructions that change the rating or the output check\n  threshold: 0/20 injection fixtures change the final rating or the output_check; 20/20 still produce\n    a valid run record\n  verification: offline profile; injected text in every retrieved-text channel (news, social, filings,\n    web)\n  semantic_part: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  - REQ-TA-FR-005\n  baseline: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified.\n    No deterministic check exists yet.\n  open: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  title: No credential or token leakage\n  type: security\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens,\n    refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n  fit_criterion: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor\n    error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions\n    finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n  tradeoff: Less debugging detail in error text.\n  metric: secret occurrences in report, log, event stream and traceback on error paths\n  threshold: 0 occurrences of any planted secret in any sink; source files unmodified\n  verification: plant 4 secret types across every sink and every error path, then scan the captured output\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`)\n    redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by the Alpha Vantage and FRED vendor modules. The boundary\n    adds `runapi/redact.py`, a `Redactor` applied at the event, report and error sinks. Coverage of third-party\n    loggers and uncaught tracebacks outside the boundary remains unverified.\n  open: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n  title: No promise of guaranteed returns\n  type: security\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed\n    profit or capital protection.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the\n    disclaimer string; (b) 5 scripted final decisions that each contain a phrase from `fixtures/sec003/guarantee_phrases.txt`\n    are checked, then 5/5 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R8.\n  tradeoff: The phrase list flags \"guaranteed\" even inside a quoted source.\n  metric: reports starting with the disclaimer, and guarantee phrases caught by rule R8\n  threshold: 20/20 reports start with the disclaimer; 5/5 guarantee fixtures get NEEDS_REVIEW with finding\n    R8\n  verification: offline profile; 20 rendered reports and 5 scripted decisions containing listed phrases\n  semantic_part: 5 live prompts that directly ask for a guarantee are in the GOV-001 suite.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  baseline: The disclaimer exists in the README only.\n  open: Add the report disclaimer and rule R8.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n  title: Vendors behind one routing point\n  type: architectural_constraint\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: Vendor access shall go through the router's method map, so agent and graph modules name a\n    method, never a vendor module or vendor SDK.\n  fit_criterion: Given `tradingagents/agents/**` and `tradingagents/graph/**`, when the import-boundary\n    test runs, then they import 0 times from `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.*` and 0 times from `yfinance`\n    (the only vendor SDK in `pyproject.toml`); and a fake vendor in the method map serves every evidence\n    request in the end-to-end test with 0 monkeypatches of agent modules.\n  tradeoff: One more indirection per call.\n  metric: direct vendor imports in agent modules\n  threshold: 0 direct vendor imports in `tradingagents/agents/**`; the layering test covers every vendor\n    package, not only `yfinance`\n  verification: static import scan anchored on the package boundary, enforced by `tests/test_layering.py`\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: 'Not met. There are 4 direct vendor imports in 3 agent files: `agents/context.py` (Yahoo profile),\n    `agents/tools.py` (Yahoo snapshot) and `agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py` (Reddit, StockTwits).\n    `tests/test_layering.py` bans only the `yfinance` library.'\n  open: Move the 4 imports behind router methods and extend the layering test.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  title: Deterministic output check\n  type: architectural_constraint\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"Exactly one deterministic, non-LLM component shall set `output_check` and `check_findings`.\\\n    \\ It runs on every `COMPLETED` run after the Portfolio Manager and applies the rules below. Each rule\\\n    \\ is owned by the requirement named in the table (P1).\\n\\n| Rule | Check | Owner | Kind |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n\\\n    | R1 | Final rating is readable (not `REVIEW`) | RUN-001 | Blocking |\\n| R2 | Every cited evidence\\\n    \\ ID resolves | FR-001 | Blocking |\\n| R3 | No banned ownership phrase | FR-007 | Blocking |\\n| R4\\\n    \\ | Sentiment score matches band | FR-008 | Blocking |\\n| R5 | Sentiment confidence within the coverage\\\n    \\ cap | FR-008 | Corrected |\\n| R6 | No sentiment direction without any sentiment data | FR-008 |\\\n    \\ Blocking |\\n| R7 | \\\"Data coverage\\\" section present and equal to the coverage record | FR-005 |\\\n    \\ Blocking |\\n| R8 | Disclaimer present; no guarantee phrase | SEC-003 | Blocking |\\n\\n## Naming (corrected\\\n    \\ 2026-11-23 after Member B's reply)\\n\\n`R1`–`R8` here means the output-check rules defined in `requirements-draft-v4.md`.\\\n    \\ Two collisions to avoid:\\n\\n- `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md` reuses the same `R`\\\n    \\ prefix for unrelated trigger rows: its `R1` is a provider failover, its `R3` is \\\"model output exhausted\\\"\\\n    . Those are not these rules.\\n- `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` emits only `Q1`–`Q4`. `R1` maps to\\\n    \\ `Q1`, `R8` maps to `Q3`/`Q4`, and `R4`–`R7` rest on coverage, sentiment and intermediate-output\\\n    \\ fields that the current checker does not inspect. `R2` has no enforcing component.\\n\\nSo this table\\\n    \\ states what a compliant system must do, not what the baseline already does.\\n\\n**Authority**: No\\\n    \\ model output can set, change or skip the check's result. Text in model output that claims a check\\\n    \\ result (\\\"validated\\\", \\\"PASSED\\\") has no effect.\\n\\n**Meaning**: `PASSED` means only that the report\\\n    \\ meets rules R1–R8. It does not mean the analysis is correct, the facts are true or the rating is\\\n    \\ good advice. The report shows this sentence next to the result.\\n\\n**Results**: any blocking finding\\\n    \\ → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; only corrected findings or none → `PASSED`; `INCOMPLETE` run → `NOT_RUN`.\\n\\n\\\n    **Failure behaviour**: If the check itself raises, the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `CHECK_ERROR`.\\\n    \\ It never falls back to `PASSED`.\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile, when (a) every `COMPLETED` fixture in Appendix A is inspected,\n    then 100% of `output_check` values equal R1–R8 applied to the final state, and the field is written\n    at exactly 1 call site in the code; (b) a fixture makes the check raise, then the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n    + `CHECK_ERROR` (1/1); (c) a fixture''s model text says \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" while R3 fails, then\n    the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` (1/1); (d) every `INCOMPLETE` fixture has `NOT_RUN` (100%).'\n  tradeoff: One more stage after the graph, and a second place a reader must look.\n  metric: authority of the output check; results set by model text\n  threshold: 0 of the injected model-text fixtures change output_check; 8/8 rules R1-R8 produce a blocking\n    finding on their failing fixture\n  verification: offline profile; inject each rule's failing fixture plus a model-text override attempt\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The deterministic check now exists:\n    `runapi/checks.py` defines `OutputChecker` with rules Q1-Q4 (rating readable, provenance matches the\n    frozen snapshot, disclaimer present, no prohibited guarantee phrase), each broken rule becoming a\n    blocking `Finding`, and `runapi/finalize.py` makes the outcome decision. `runapi/reporting.py` verifies\n    the envelope header against the trusted input. What remains unverified is enforcement on every enabled\n    entry point: the raw `TradingAgentsGraph` primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path, and the Portfolio\n    Manager still writes its rating directly (`agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`).'\n  open: Member B designs the component and documents the authority and failure rules above.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n  note: 'Rules R1-R8 are the OUTPUT-CHECK rules defined in requirements-draft-v4.md. Naming, corrected\n    2026-11-23 after Member B''s reply, to avoid a collision in the team''s documents: `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`\n    uses the same `R` prefix for unrelated trigger rows (its R1 is a provider failover, its R3 is model\n    exhausted), and `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` emits only `Q1`-`Q4`. R1 maps to Q1, R8 to Q3/Q4;\n    R4-R7 rest on coverage, sentiment and intermediate-output fields that this requirement set defines\n    and the current checker does not inspect, and R2 has no enforcing component. So R1-R8 state what a\n    compliant system must do, not what the baseline does. Identity rule and result mapping are unchanged.'\n- id: REQ-TA-INV-001\n  title: Unreadable rating never passes\n  type: invariant\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: The system shall hold that a final rating that cannot be parsed is reported as `REVIEW` with\n    `output_check = NEEDS_REVIEW`, and `PASSED` is never claimed for a run whose final rating is `REVIEW`.\n    This does not claim that every `COMPLETED` run yields a usable investment rating, and it does not\n    make `REVIEW` a model failure.\n  zero_tolerance: true\n  enforced_by: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  rule_owner: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  amended_by: []\n  fit_criterion: Given the unreadable-rating fixtures, when each is checked, then 100% are reported `COMPLETED`\n    + `REVIEW` + `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1); 0 REPORT a `REVIEW` rating under `PASSED`. A single observed\n    violation is 1 blocking defect; no run is exempt.\n  tradeoff: A zero-tolerance invariant fails the build on one counterexample, which costs time when the\n    counterexample is a fixture bug rather than a product bug.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  note: 'Promoted 2026-11-23 (A-10) from ARCH-002''s rule table; source requirement RUN-001. LAYERS (OQ-7,\n    revised 2026-11-23): this entry owns the requirement meaning and its zero-tolerance fit criterion.\n    Member B''s `docs/architecture/invariants.md` owns the architecture enforcement, runtime monitor and\n    fallback. Neither document overrides the other. Crosswalk to B''s register (B''s reply of 2026-11-23):",

Scores follow EVAL-001's counting\\\n1287:     \\ rules.\\n\\n**Start-up rule**: Until Member D fixes `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` from a baseline measurement,\\\n1288:     \\ the job runs and reports but does not block merges.\"\n1289:   fit_criterion: Given `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` is fixed, when a PR touches a file in `GOV_PATHS`, then the\n1290:     job runs 1 time and a score below `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` fails a required check (merge blocked). A PR\n1291:     touching no such path skips the job without blocking.\n1292:   tradeoff: Every prompt edit pays evaluation time and API cost.\n1293:   metric: whether a prompt/model change can merge without passing the semantic suite\n1294:   threshold: 0 merges touching GOV_PATHS without a suite run once QUALITY_THRESHOLD is fixed; a below-threshold\n1295:     score blocks the merge\n1296:   verification: CI job inspection plus one deliberately failing score fixture\n1297:   dependencies: []\n1298:   baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. CI runs pytest, a clean-install smoke\n1299:     test and strict ruff (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); no requirement-registry validation step exists\n1300:     yet. A semantic evaluation exists outside CI: `docs/verification/semantic-evaluation.md` (GOV-004)\n1301:     and `docs/architecture/evaluation-table.md`, with recorded evidence under `docs/reviews/evidence/`.'\n1302:   open: Define the cases and rubric; fix the parameters.\n1303:   source:\n1304:   - kind: team_document\n1305:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n1306:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n1307:     locator: REQ-TA-GOV-001\n1308:   - kind: baseline_observation\n1309:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n1310:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n1311: - id: REQ-TA-GOV-002\n1312:   title: Test plan approved before implementation\n1313:   type: governance\n1314:   priority: Must\n1315:   status: proposed\n1316:   statement: \"Before implementation begins, the test plan for a changed feature shall carry an attributable\\\n1317:     \\ human approval record covering the approved test scope and the plan revision approved; an implementation\\\n1318:     \\ pull request shall not merge otherwise.\\n\\n**Record (format confirmed by Member E, 2026-11-23; mechanism\\\n1319:     \\ not yet implemented).** One YAML file per approval under `docs/verification/approvals/`, uniquely\\\n1320:     \\ named where a feature has several approvals or revisions, with superseded evidence preserved. Minimum\\\n1321:     \\ fields: `approver`, `approver_role`, `approved_at` with timezone, `plan_ref`, `plan_sha256`, `scope`\\\n1322:     \\ (the covered requirement or feature IDs), `approval_evidence_ref` (the retained human confirmation)\\\n1323:     \\ and `approval_commit` (the revision holding the approved plan and the record). A GitHub account\\\n1324:     \\ name maps to a named team member. A bot-generated file is never human approval.\\n\\n**Rules.** The\\\n1325:     \\ approval revision must be an ancestor of the first implementation commit for the declared scope;\\\n1326:     \\ a self-entered timestamp is not sufficient proof, and ancestry is evidence of ordering only, never\\\n1327:     \\ of when coding actually began or of genuine human review. The plan hash is checked against the plan\\\n1328:     \\ at the approved revision. An approval never extends to a materially changed plan or to an unlisted\\\n1329:     \\ feature without renewed approval. No hotfix, single-member or approver-absence exception exists.\\\n1330:     \\ A later passing test run or a CI receipt cannot substitute for a missing prior approval. Historical\\\n1331:     \\ work without evidence is disclosed as an evidence gap, never backdated or retrospectively described\\\n1332:     \\ as prior approval.\"\n1333:   fit_criterion: 'Given an implementation pull request, when its approval check runs, then (a) a valid\n1334:     record with all 8 fields, a human evidence reference, a matching `plan_sha256` and a covering `scope`\n1335:     whose `approval_commit` is an ancestor of the first implementation commit passes with 0 blocking findings;\n1336:     and (b) each of 5 negative fixtures fails with exactly 1 blocking finding: record absent, record incomplete,\n1337:     approval commit not an ancestor, plan hash or scope mismatch, and an approval claim with no human\n1338:     evidence.'\n1339:   tradeoff: The approval record is an extra artefact to maintain and keep attributable before any code\n1340:     is written.\n1341:   metric: approval records traceable to a commit on the approved history\n1342:   threshold: 100% of approval records name the approver, the commit and the artefact version; 100% of\n1343:     approved commits are ancestors of the approving branch head\n1344:   verification: audit every approval record against the commit graph; attempt a rebased rewrite and confirm\n1345:     it is detected\n1346:   dependencies: []\n1347:   baseline: Not present; this is a process rule, not a product feature.\n1348:   open: Team and course decision on the record format.\n1349:   source:\n1350:   - kind: team_document\n1351:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n1352:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n1353:     locator: REQ-TA-GOV-002\n1354:   - kind: baseline_observation\n1355:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n1356:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n1357:   - kind: team_document\n1358:     ref: cs5351-2026-2027-project.pdf\n1359:     locator: p10 gate 1\n1360:   - kind: team_document\n1361:     ref: cs5351-2026-2027-project.pdf\n1362:     locator: p6 D1(transcript), p7 D9\n1363:   note: 'OQ-3, closed 2026-11-23 on Member E''s reply. The record format v4 left open as ''team and course\n1364:     decision'' is now stated. Two corrections to A''s own earlier wording. First, A had proposed switching\n1365:     the ordering check from timestamps to commit ancestry; E''s answer is that ancestry is the repository-ordering\n1366:     check only and proves neither that coding began later nor that a human approved the tests, and both\n1367:     the requirement and the evidence must say so. Second, E proposed replacing this requirement with post-implementation\n1368:     CI receipts; E has since checked course page 10 gate 1 and the transcript requirements on pages 6\n1369:     and 7, withdrawn that proposal, and will implement this gate. That replacement wording is recorded\n1370:     as withdrawn, not adopted. Status is `proposed`, not `implemented`: E states that the mechanism and\n1371:     its positive and negative checks are not yet built, and neither this reply nor the course citation\n1372:     is the team''s signed adoption record.'\n1373: - id: REQ-TA-GOV-003\n1374:   title: AI-use log updated before merge\n1375:   type: governance\n1376:   priority: Must\n1377:   status: proposed\n1378:   statement: A pull request that changes code or prompts shall be blocked unless the AI-use log has been\n1379:     updated for that change. The log records the real tools, models and interventions used; it is not\n1380:     a retyped summary. The gate checks that an update exists in the pull request; it does not validate\n1381:     the log's format or prose except where a separately agreed rule says so.\n1382:   fit_criterion: Given a pull request that changes a file under the governed code or prompt paths, when\n1383:     the AI-use log gate runs, then (a) 1 accepted fixture with an updated log passes with 0 findings;\n1384:     (b) 1 rejected fixture without an update fails with exactly 1 blocking finding; and (c) a pull request\n1385:     that touches only files outside those paths is not blocked, 0 findings.\n1386:   dependencies: []\n1387:   tradeoff: A mandatory log edit on every code or prompt change adds friction; it is accepted because\n1388:     the course names this gate explicitly.\n1389:   amended_by: []\n1390:   note: 'Added 2026-11-23 on Member E''s E14. Course page 10 gate 6 names it as a blocking gate, and page\n1391:     9 lists `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as the D7 blocking-gate pipeline, so it belongs in the registry,\n1392:     not only in repository process. None of this is implemented: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`\n1395:     at `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb` has three jobs (tests, smoke-install, lint) and no AI-log or dependency\n1396:     gate. E states the update-only policy stays; format and content validation are explicitly not requested.'\n1397:   source:\n1398:   - kind: team_document\n1399:     ref: cs5351-2026-2027-project.pdf\n1400:     locator: p10 gate 6, p9 ci.yml\n1401:   - kind: team_document\n1402:     ref: docs/req/selected-requirements.md\n1403:     locator: SEL-TA-GOV-005\n1404: fixture_profiles:\n1405:   note: 'Added 2026-11-23 to correct a contradiction in A''s own Appendix A. The offline profile pinned\n1406:     `Portfolio: None (research-only scope)` while 11 test modules supply a portfolio and test_nfr003_privacy.py\n1407:     plants a second position that cannot exist without one. Terminal-append failure alone still preserves the logical outcome with `terminal_event.durable=false`; report/manifest remain critical and the single-terminal rule is preserved.\n \n+## Implementation status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n+\n+The C2 boundary is present in the checkout, not merely designed:\n+\n+- `runapi/input_service.py` (`PortfolioInputService`, `freeze_explicit`, `freeze_no_portfolio`), `runapi/context.py` (`RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, `ConsentState`), `runapi/execution.py` (`run_analysis_api`, rejects non-`CONFIRMED` at `:149`), `runapi/checks.py` (`OutputChecker`, Q1–Q4), `runapi/finalize.py` (`classify_exception`, `OutcomeFinalizer`), `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename` publication at `:154`), `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal), `runapi/result.py` (`RunResult`/`CheckResult`/`Finding`), `runapi/reporting.py` (`build_envelope`, `verify_envelope_header_matches`), `runapi/redact.py`.\n+- R1–R5 repairs are implemented (`agents/structured.py` applies the shared `Redactor` to its fallback warnings). Independent acceptance of these repairs remains **pending (C)**; the implementation's own remediation record is `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n+- The C-owned tests under `tests/member_c_verification/offline/` define the seams; passing status is C's to report, not this ADR's.\n+\n+## Proposed broader requirements — impact, **not** implemented\n+\n+The uploaded `requirements.yaml` (`status: proposed_for_adoption`) and A's later correspondence would extend the as-built system. If adopted, the following are architecture impacts, documented but **not** designed as accepted decisions here:\n+\n+- **`BUDGET` stop reason** and a run-wide **single-use call-reservation** controller (`REQ-TA-RUN-001`, `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`): would add a sixth serialized `StopReason`, a shared budget component consulted before every model dispatch, and updates to every reader. The current five-value literal (`runapi/result.py:12-14`) has no `BUDGET`.\n+- **R1–R8 output check** (`REQ-TA-ARCH-002`) and **corrected-only `PASSED`** (R5): R2 (evidence-ID resolution) and R4–R7 (sentiment/coverage) require new data fields and registry components the checker does not inspect; R5 would change `Finding.status`/`CheckResult` so `PASSED` can carry corrected findings — a coordinated type change across checks/report/scorer if retained.\n+- **Evidence and coverage registries** (`REQ-TA-FR-001`, `REQ-TA-FR-005`, `REQ-TA-INV-002/007`), **aggregate budgets/resume** (`REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002`, `COST-001/002`, D-5): new components and a resume contract that currently conflicts with `INV-11`/`INV-12`.\n+- **`REQ-TA-INV-014` / `REQ-TA-GOV-004`** are pending publication; the existing design already covers input freezing (`INV-04/05/05b`) and treats schema validation as a governance/CI boundary, so their absence does not change C2's data flow.\n+\n ## Reopening conditions\n \n - Instructor mandates a single orchestration façade → revisit C3.\n - File-count/scope constraints favour C1 → revisit.\n",
