        "file": "docs/architecture/permission-model.md",
        "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/permission-model.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/permission-model.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/permission-model.md\t\n@@ -1,68 +1,68 @@\n # Permission Model (Member B design)\n \n-Status: architecture draft (revised 2026-11-12 per review B3-06; implementation-aligned 2026-11-24). Describes **application roles during a run** and **per-coding-agent-role file rights**, kept separate. E implements enforcement. As of `a62b801`, governance **tooling and policy files exist** (`docs/code-governance/`, `scripts/ci/`, `.github/workflows/`), but the OpenCode permission package (`AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc`, `.agent/`) is **still absent**, so no OpenCode permission enforcement is installed. Per the 24 November integration review, the public integration branch requires only four checks (`ai-log updated`, `dependency check`, `required tests`, `ruff`); `test approval` is implemented but **not a required merge check**, and PR 16 merged with a failed approval check. This draft claims **no** demonstrated denial and **no** enforced fifth gate. See `risk-list.md` R-GOV.\n+Status: architecture draft (revised 2026-11-12 per review B3-06; implementation-aligned 2026-11-24). Describes **application roles during a run** and **per-coding-agent-role file rights**, kept separate. E implements enforcement. As of `a62b801`, governance **tooling and policy files exist** (`docs/code-governance/`, `scripts/ci/`, `.github/workflows/`), but the OpenCode permission package (`AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc`, `.agent/`) is **still absent**, so no OpenCode permission enforcement is installed. **Governance status (corrected 2026-11-24), per the integration review `evidence/integration-review-2026-11-24/github-checks.json`:** the public integration branch **requires** `ai-log updated`, `dependency check`, `required tests`, `ruff (strict, full repo)` — so **AI-use-log updates are a required merge check**. The **test-approval tooling exists and runs**, but **merge enforcement remains incomplete**: `test approval` is **not** in the required-status-check contexts, and PR 16 merged with a failed approval check. This draft claims **no** demonstrated denial and **no** enforced approval gate; schema-validation gating is likewise not wired. See `risk-list.md` R-GOV.\n \n Source: `SEL-TA-GOV-006` (B permission design; E enforcement). Ownership follows the team allocation recorded in `docs/architecture/evaluation-logbook.md`; the previously cited `docs/project-deliverables-and-ownership.md` is **not present** in the checkout.\n \n ## 1. Role separation\n \n | Role | Who | Reads | Writes |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | **End user (application)** | Terminal user | Their selected portfolio file (via the service); own reports/logs | Reports/logs/manifest under results dir; never secrets |\n | **Application runtime** | Process during a run | The one frozen snapshot; own inputs | Results artifacts, event sink, manifest (write-once) |\n | **Coding agent** | OpenCode acting for A/B/C/D/E | Per-role whitelist (below) | Per-role whitelist (below) |\n | **Human reviewer** | Team/E | Per course | Governance/CI config, final assembly |\n \n Application roles and coding-agent roles are not conflated: a run gains no development permissions; a coding agent gains no access to real holdings.\n \n ## 2. Per coding-agent-role profiles (default-deny)\n \n Deny precedence: **deny wins** over any allow; a more-specific deny overrides a broader allow. All roles: **never readable** `.env`, `.env.enterprise*`, auth/token stores, real portfolio files, logs with real holdings, `.venv`, home-directory config, Git credential data; **symlink escapes excluded** consistently for every role. **Human-only (no coding agent writes):** `.opencode/rules.md`.\n \n ### 2.1 Common startup READ set (all coding-agent roles) — F5\n Every coding-agent role must read the governance/blueprint startup set; these paths are **readable by all A/B/C/D/E** (still subject to the secret denies above):\n ```\n AGENTS.md, Prompt.md, architecture-blueprint.md, docs/architecture/**,\n docs/project-deliverables-and-ownership.md (if present; currently absent from the checkout)\n ```\n This makes the startup reading order runnable under default-deny without opening secret paths.\n \n ### 2.2 Role write/extra-read profiles\n | Role (owner) | Writable (in-role) | Extra reads (beyond common) | Explicitly denied writable | Phase approval |\n |---|---|---|---|---|\n | **A — Requirements** | `docs/req/**` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**` | everything else writable (arch/code/tests/governance) | A publishes final D1 |\n | **B — Architecture** | approved B set: root `architecture-blueprint.md`, `docs/architecture/adr/**`, the 13 approved architecture files | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `docs/req/**` | `docs/req/**`, `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `Report.md`, `.github/**`, `.agent/**`, `.opencode/**`, **`docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` (E-owned)**, review docs, transcripts | approved write plan |\n | **C — Verification** | `tests/**`, `docs/verification/**`, `docs/review-memo.md`, `docs/bug-diary.md`, `docs/debt-register.md` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `docs/req/**` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `docs/req/**`, architecture (read only), governance/CI, transcripts | test-plan approval (GOV-001) before impl |\n | **D — Implementation** | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `prompts/**`, `docs/experiments/**` | `tests/**` (read), `docs/req/**` | **`tests/**` writes (does NOT auto-receive test-write)**, `docs/req/**`, architecture (read only), governance/CI, `.opencode/rules.md`, transcripts | C's approved tests; E's gates |\n | **E — Governance** | `AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` (not `rules.md`), `.github/**`, `docs/code-governance/**`, **`docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` (E-owned)**, `docs/ai-use-log.yaml`, `transcripts/index.md`, `README.md`, `Report.md` (final edit), `docs/submission/**`, `submission/**` | everything (read), subject to secret denies | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `docs/req/**`, the 13 B-owned architecture files (**B-owned; E collects, does not edit**), `prompts/**` | human-authorized |\n \n **Trace-matrix authority (F5):** E is the **sole writer** of `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md`; it is **removed from B's writable deny set only in E's column** and is **not** in B's writable set. To reconcile deny precedence, the file has exactly one owning role (E) with an explicit write allow; no other role (including B) has a writable allow for it, and any broad deny applied to `docs/architecture/**` for other roles simply keeps it unwritable for them. E's broad read is enumerated by the common startup set (§2.1) plus the role's own/governance paths — not a vague \"everything\".\n \n **Covenant/verification ownership:** `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` → owner **C** (write); `.agent/rules.md` → owner **E**; `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` → owner **E**. Every required governance/covenant file has one authorized writer; none defaults to nobody.\n \n **Critical rule (B3-06):** D running the coding agent does **not** automatically receive write authority over `tests/**`. Test writes by D require an **explicit, recorded extra authorization** (E-recorded, human-approved exception with rationale), preserving C's independent-verification separation. The same recording applies if roles rotate.\n \n ## 3. Application-run data policy (separate from coding agents)\n \n - `PORTFOLIO_DIR` defaults to `<project-root>/portfolios`; discovery **non-recursive**, regular `.json`, deterministic filename order, **symlinks excluded**. Do not search home/credentials/arbitrary folders.\n - Explicit `--portfolio PATH` may point outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned.\n - Selected file read **once**, frozen; not re-read after freeze; source read-only.\n - Secrets never emitted; central `Redactor` masks keys/OAuth access+refresh tokens/bearer [REDACTED]\n \n ## 4. Enforcement (E) and denied-write behaviour (GOV-006)\n \n - **Present at `a62b801`:** `docs/code-governance/{verification-constraints.md,test-approval-policy.yaml,self-review-workflow.md,dependency-*}`; CI helpers in `scripts/ci/` (`check_test_approval.py`, `check_ai_log_updated.py`, `check_required_tests.py`, `check_dependencies.py`, `build_pr_self_review.py`); workflows `.github/workflows/{ci,test-approval,test-approval-complete,pr-self-review,release-assets}.yml`.\n - **Absent / not enforced:** the OpenCode permission package (`AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc`, `.opencode/rules.md`, `.agent/rules.md`) is not present, so per-role file rights below are **design intent only**. The public integration branch lists only four required checks; `test approval` exists but is **not required**, and a PR merged with a failed approval check (24 November review, I24 03). Schema-validation gating is likewise not wired.\n - E wires per-role whitelists into `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` and CI. A denied access attempt must be **blocked and logged without changing the file**. This draft does **not** claim a demonstrated denial or an enforced fifth gate.\n - Branch protection is *intended* to require passing checks + human review + ADR for safety changes; the review found full admin-only settings not verifiable and `test approval` not required. B's ADRs remain the architecture contribution.\n \n ## 5. Permitted/denied examples (document examples) — F5\n - **Startup reads:** A/B/C/D/E can all read `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `architecture-blueprint.md`, `docs/architecture/**` → permitted.\n - **E writes `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md`** → permitted (E sole owner); **B writes it** → denied.\n - **D writes `tests/test_output_check.py`** → **denied** (D lacks test-write) unless an E-recorded extra authorization exists.\n - **C writes `tests/...`** → permitted (C owns tests).\n - **Any agent edits `.opencode/rules.md`** → **denied** (human-only).\n - **Any agent reads `.env` or a real portfolio file** → denied.\n \n ## 6. Out of scope\n No exposure/account validation, no broker credentials handling, no new web auth surface. No claim of installed governance.\n",

        "deletions": 1,
        "status": "modified"

        "file": "docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md",
        "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,237 @@\n+# Staged implementation prompt pack (Member B) — UNEXECUTED TEMPLATES\n+\n+Status: **unexecuted templates, 2026-11-24.** These are drafting artifacts for a *future* implementation handoff. **Architecture approval does not authorize code implementation.** Each slice's execution plan and test criteria still require prior human approval before any build, and the model-provider access constraint is stated below. No template here has been run; no code, tests, approvals or results are claimed.\n+\n+Scope of these templates: the prioritised slices in [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §13–§16 and [ADR 002](../adr/002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md):\n+- **Slice C — run budget controller + `BUDGET`** (first handoff; §15).\n+- **Slice A — evidence & coverage** (§13).\n+- **Slice B — output-check v2 R1–R8** (§14).\n+\n+**Model access constraint (access, not a mandate).** As of drafting, DeepSeek V4 Flash is the only model available to Member B's OpenCode work via the school API key. This is an access constraint for this implementation route; it is **not** a course requirement, an evaluated model choice, or a restriction on TradingAgents' inherited provider capabilities. Do not commit/push.\n+```\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Template 4 — Verification prompt (checks, outcomes, negatives, evidence)\n+\n+```\n+You are verifying an implemented, approved slice in CS5351. Do not\n+modify application code or the implementation's tests to make them pass.\n+\n+Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n+Approved plan/acceptance revision/hash: <from Template 2/3>\n+\n+CHECKS TO RUN (offline; scripted model; record exact commands + results):\n+- Targeted slice tests, then the prior offline suite, Ruff, dependency and\n+  whitespace checks. Use the project virtual environment; no paid/live calls.\n+- Positive cases: each approved scenario passes.\n+- NEGATIVE cases (must fail as designed):\n+    C_budget: >CALL_CAP attempts admitted; exhaustion swallowed by fallback;\n+      shared counter across runs; budget relabelled INTERNAL_ERROR; BUDGET stop\n+      overriding a co-occurring persistence failure.\n+    A_evidence_coverage: dangling cited ID passes; unrequested channel mislabelled\n+      as gap; core-gap completes; coverage section differs under prose change.\n+    B_checker_v2: CORRECTED treated as NEEDS_REVIEW; BLOCKING treated as PASSED;\n+      Q2 and R2 conflated; R3 phrase downgraded to corrected; model \"PASSED\" text\n+      overriding a blocking rule.\n+- Compatibility: a reader that enumerates old StopReason / old finding status\n+  fails closed on the new value (not silent coercion); schema_version behavior.\n+\n+EXPECTED OUTCOMES: state precisely per case (counters, fields, status, stop_reason,\n+output_check, paths null/not-null). Maps each supported failure/degraded path to trigger, responsible component, fallback/action, output and diagnostic/monitor, consistent with the selected result/check contract (`SEL-TA-FR-007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001`). Components exist in the `a62b801` checkout (verified); test evidence is C's; enforcement wiring is D/E's. No measured results are claimed.\n \n > **Label namespace warning:** the `R1`, `R2`, … in the **first column of the table below are trigger-row identifiers in this catalog only**. They are **not** the output-check rules `R1–R8` of proposed `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`, and **not** the checker codes `Q1–Q4` in `runapi/checks.py`. For example, catalog `R1` here is a recoverable-data sentinel path, whereas `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`'s `R1` is \"final rating readable\". Do not equate them by number.\n \n ## Result contract reminder\n - `run_outcome = COMPLETED | INCOMPLETE`.\n - `COMPLETED`: graph returned; final `rating ∈ {Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, REVIEW}`.\n - `INCOMPLETE`: no final rating; `stop_reason ∈ {MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED}`.\n - `output_check = PASSED | NEEDS_REVIEW | NOT_RUN`; incomplete ⇒ NOT_RUN.\n - Progress vocabulary (events) is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n \n | # | Trigger | Responsible component | Fallback / action | Output | Diagnostic / monitor |\n |---|---|---|---|---|---|\n | R1 | Recoverable non-core data unavailable (upstream sentinel) | Engine/tools (baseline behaviour preserved) | Continue run with the sentinel/absent marker; **do not** classify fatal | COMPLETED (or normal) | Event notes degraded node; **not** an incomplete reason |\n | R2 | Structured-output invocation fails, free text usable | `structured.py` path → PM text fallback | Use free-text; parse rating deterministically; the warning's exception detail is passed through the shared `Redactor` before logging (R1) | COMPLETED; rating if readable else REVIEW | Existing structured-fallback warning retained, redacted |\n | R3 | Model/provider output exhausted | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; no final rating | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE` | `event=run.terminal`; redacted cause |\n | R4 | Raised vendor/data exception (unrecovered) | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; typed result | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=DATA_FAILURE` | Redacted data exception message |\n | R5 | Ordinary internal exception | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; typed result, no escape past public entry | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` | Redacted traceback summary |\n | R6 | Malformed/invalid portfolio input | `runapi/input_service.py` (precheck + upstream model) | Stop **before dispatch**; filename + bad field/path, no contents/credentials | No run (pre-run rejection) | Input diagnostic; zero LLM calls |\n | R7 | As-of mismatch (`--portfolio-as-of` ≠ analysis date) | `runapi/input_service.py` | Stop before dispatch | Pre-run input error | Field-level diagnostic |\n | R8 | Selected file changed after confirmation | (no reread) | **Ignore** changed bytes; use frozen snapshot | Normal run with frozen identity | (no silent change; provenance records frozen digest) |\n | R9 | Output check rule broken (Q1–Q4) | `runapi/checks.py` | Do not pass; mark review needed | If graph returned: COMPLETED + NEEDS_REVIEW + blocking finding(s) | `event=output.check` findings |\n | R10 | Checker raises exception | `runapi/checks.py` (fail closed) | Blocking `CHECK_ERROR` | COMPLETED retained if graph returned, but NEEDS_REVIEW | `event=output.check` `CHECK_ERROR` |\n | R11 | Model text claims \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" but a rule fails | `runapi/checks.py` authority | Model claim ignored | NEEDS_REVIEW | Authority-source tag on check event |\n | R12 | Cooperative cancellation | `runapi/execution` + CLI coordinator | Stop cooperatively (if during run) or zero-start (pre-run) | Pre-run: no completed run; during run: INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERRUPTED` | `event=input.consent`/`run.terminal` |\n | R13a | Critical report/manifest staging or commit failure before rename (terminal-event append excluded) | `runapi/persist.py` + `runapi/finalize.py` | No rename; nothing visible at published path; revise logical outcome | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null` | Redacted persistence diagnostic; `_staging` not treated as published | \n | R13b | Best-effort sink failure (state JSON or message log) | `runapi/persist.py` | Continue; redacted note; does not flip a completed decision | Normal outcome unchanged | Redacted note | \n | R14 | Terminal-event JSONL append to staging fails (best-effort, non-critical) | `runapi/events.py` | Commit still publishes; logical outcome preserved (not PERSISTENCE_ERROR); manifest states non-durable terminal | Normal logical outcome; `terminal_event.durable=false` in manifest | Redacted diagnostic; later progress append never changes manifest | \n | R13c | Critical report/manifest staging/commit failure (R13a) after a tentative terminal was staged (R5) | `runapi/events.py` + `runapi/persist.py` + `runapi/execution.py` | Discard the stage-private tentative terminal; never expose a caller-visible COMPLETED; emit exactly one INCOMPLETE terminal matching the returned result | INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR/NOT_RUN; single INCOMPLETE terminal in caller sink | Redacted persistence diagnostic; no stale COMPLETED |\n | R15 | Workflow returns unreadable final text | `runapi/finalize.py` + `runapi/checks.py` | Complete with REVIEW | COMPLETED + rating REVIEW + NEEDS_REVIEW | Q1 finding |\n | R16 | Same-ticker/date second fresh run | `runapi/persist.py` / coordinator (run-ID isolation) | Write to a **new** run dir; refuse overwrite of prior artifacts | New isolated artifacts; first run unchanged | `event=output.persist` |\n \n ## Ordering and conditions\n - Every incomplete result has `output_check=NOT_RUN`; every completed result has a rating (REVIEW allowed) and a check result.\n - `MODEL_FAILURE` is used **only** for exhausted model/provider output failures; recoverable optional-data sentinels (R1) are never reclassified as fatal.\n - Diagnostics are redacted (NFR-003) before delivery; secrets/holdings never appear.\n - Durability across total disk failure/power loss is **not** promised; PERSISTENCE_ERROR is the cooperative failure contract.\n \n ## As-built status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n Rows R3–R5 (`MODEL_FAILURE`/`DATA_FAILURE`/`INTERNAL_ERROR`) and R12 (`INTERRUPTED`) map to `runapi/finalize.py::classify_exception`; R13a/R13c/R14 map to `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename`, truthful `terminal_event.durable`) and `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal). I approve architecture drafting under the expanded plan, with these corrections:

1. Design the published proposed target for R5: corrected findings may coexist with PASSED; blocking findings produce NEEDS_REVIEW. Correct the verification scenarios accordingly. Record deferral only as an unapproved requirements-change alternative.
2. Retain the proposed blocking R3 phrase-check target. Document contextual handling as an alternative requiring A/C/team agreement, not an advisory replacement.
3. Preserve the existing Q2 trusted-provenance guard separately from evidence-ID R2.
4. Agree evidence/coverage data contracts before dependent R2/R7 checker integration. You may prioritize the budget handoff, including its necessary result/configuration/report/manifest/scorer compatibility changes.
5. Correct governance status: AI-log updates are required; test-approval tooling exists but merge enforcement remains incomplete.
6. Label feasibility estimates and unresolved adoption decisions explicitly.

Produce implementation-ready contracts, sequences, failure/concurrency policies and concrete proposed test scenarios. Preserve the original C2 history; record genuine new design decisions separately.

This approves architecture documents only—not application/test implementation or final requirements adoption. Keep the attribution/privacy corrections proportionate. Finish with the design handoff, remaining decisions and checks actually performed.

Also deliver a staged implementation prompt pack for each design slice, suitable for another member to use with OpenCode and the available DeepSeek V4 Flash model.

Include:
1. A read-only planning prompt referencing the requirements, architecture contracts and baseline revision.
2. A human checkpoint for approving the execution plan and test criteria.
3. A build prompt with explicit permitted files, interfaces, examples, acceptance criteria and scope limits.
4. A verification prompt specifying checks, expected outcomes, negative cases and evidence to retain.
5. Review and escalation conditions for failures or changes outside the approved scope.

Label these as unexecuted templates. Architecture approval does not authorize code implementation; the code-stage plan and tests still require prior human approval.

Feasibility of implementing it before 25 Nov is **not promised** (see §16).\n\n### 13.1 Proposed components and module boundaries\n| Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner(design/impl/test/enforce) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `EvidenceRegistry` | Assign stable evidence IDs; retain per-item records; expose lookup for citation resolution | `tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py` | B / D / C / E |\n| `CoverageTracker` | Accumulate one code per channel; classify core/non-core; compute `NOT_REQUESTED`; render deterministic section | `tradingagents/runapi/coverage.py` | B / D / C / E |\n| Router/bypass seams | Emit a record/code for every channel, including the 2 router-bypass channels (3 and 11) | `tradingagents/dataflows/router.py` (+ bypass call sites) | B / D / C / E |\n\nDependency rule preserved: `runapi/*` must not import `cli`.\n\n### 13.2 Field-level data contracts (authority noted per field)\n\n```\nEvidenceRecord {\n  evidence_id: str            # stable within a run; assigned by EvidenceRegistry (AUTHORITATIVE, deterministic)\n  channel: ChannelCode        # see §13.3 (deterministic)\n  source: str                 # vendor/source label as supplied (SOURCE-PROVIDED metadata; not model text)\n  ticker: str                 # instrument the item concerns (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  observed_at: str | null     # ISO-8601 when observed, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  published_at: str | null    # ISO-8601 publication/filing date, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  as_of_window: str           # the FR-004 window this item was admitted under (deterministic)\n  value_ref: str | null       # opaque pointer to the retained payload; NOT the payload text (deterministic)\n}\n```\n\n- **Invariant:** at least one of `observed_at` / `published_at` is non-null for every admitted item (R2 resolution depends on it). Enforced by `EvidenceRegistry` on admission.\n- **IDs are run-scoped** and never derived from model output. A citation in the rendered report references `evidence_id`; R2 (§14) resolves it against the registry.\n- **Retention vs outage:** records are written to the run's own artifact area. \"Retain evidence after an ordinary engine failure\" is **not** a promise that storage succeeds during a critical persistence outage; on critical report/manifest failure the run is `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and no published paths are promised (§7.3). Evidence retention is best-effort relative to that critical boundary.\n\n```\nCoverageRecord {\n  channel: ChannelCode        # 12 channels (§13.3)\n  code: \"OK\" | \"UNAVAILABLE\" | \"NO_DATA\" | \"STALE\" | \"WITHHELD\" | \"NOT_REQUESTED\"   # (deterministic)\n  detail: str | null          # redacted, source-metadata-derived; never model prose\n}\nCoverageSet {\n  entries: CoverageRecord[12]         # exactly one row per channel (deterministic)\n  core_channels: ChannelCode[]        # e.g. price family; configurable, default per requirement\n  run_core_ok: bool                   # all core channels == OK\n}\n```\n\n- **Coverage is built from tool results, never written by the model.** The rendered \"Data coverage\" section is produced deterministically from `CoverageSet`; R7 (§14) asserts the rendered section equals the record.\n- `NOT_REQUESTED` = no selected analyst asked for this channel and no vendor call was made; valid for both COMPLETED and INCOMPLETE.\n- **Core rule:** any core channel ≠ `OK` ⇒ run ends `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`. Non-core gaps do not stop the run.\n\n### 13.3 Channel enumeration (12) and bypass handling\nChannels map to the router method map. **Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router** in the baseline and require explicit emission at their call sites (D must confirm the exact channel↔method mapping against `router.py` and the two bypass paths before implementation). The enum is a design proposal; the exact membership and the two bypass indices are **to be confirmed by D/C** against the real code (see §16 decision D5).\n\n### 13.4 Freshness (§`REQ-TA-FR-006`) — proposed parameters\n- Price freshness: latest bar ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` (10, fixed) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ core gap ⇒ `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`.\n- Statement freshness: filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional, **open**) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ coded `STALE`, shown with filing date, run continues.\n- News/social: item inside the *D*-clamped window; excluded items are `NO_DATA`/`UNAVAILABLE`, not `STALE`.\n- `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` is a **configuration decision, not a measured value** (open; A owns).\n\n### 13.5 Normal sequence\n`admit(item) → assign evidence_id + record in EvidenceRegistry → set/refine CoverageRecord[channel]` for each retrieved item; at finalize, `coverage = CoverageSet.compute()` and `coverage.render()` produces the report section. Sequence integrates at the data boundary (`router`/bypass), before the checker runs.\n\n### 13.6 Failure / concurrency / privacy / persistence policy\n- **Failure:** a malformed item that cannot be admitted is a data error for that channel (coded), not a crash; core-gap ⇒ `DATA_FAILURE`.\n- **Concurrency:** analysts fan out; `EvidenceRegistry` and `CoverageTracker` mutations must be thread-safe (single lock per registry/tracker, or per-thread accumulation merged at join). IDs must remain unique under concurrency.\n- **Privacy:** records carry source metadata and an opaque `value_ref`, not raw payloads; redaction applies at any sink that emits records; holdings/other-position content never enters an evidence record.\n- **Persistence:** evidence/coverage are written into the run's artifact area; a critical publication failure does not promise their durability beyond §7.3; on ordinary engine failure, retained records stay available if storage worked.\n\n### 13.7 Compatibility/migration\nAdditive fields only. Existing manifests gain `coverage` and (optionally) an evidence index reference; `schema_version` bumps. Old readers must tolerate the new fields (forward-compatible) or a version gate applies. Run-wide request-budget boundary — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002` + `BUDGET` (PROPOSED; prioritized first handoff)\n\nStatus: **proposed implementation-ready design**, consolidating `docs/architecture/proposals/reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md` and the stop-reason reply. **Not implemented.** This is the **first recommended implementation handoff** (§16): most isolated, offline-testable, unblocks a Must (`COST-002`) plus RUN-001's `BUDGET`.\n\n### 15.1 Component and boundary\n| Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `RunBudgetController` | One per run; issues single-use reservations; enforces `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; exposes exhausted state | `tradingagents/runapi/budget.py` | B / D / C / E |\n\n- The controller lives at the **controlled application client boundary** (where the app issues model-request attempts), shared across quick/deep tiers, structured/plain paths, retries and in-run memory/reflection. It must **not** be a global counter across runs; it must be **separate from the frozen input snapshot** (`RunContext`).\n- `CALL_CAP` is a **configuration value** (test value 8; production default open, **not a measured value**).\n\n### 15.2 Interface (proposed signatures)\n```\nclass RunBudgetExhausted(Exception): ...     # distinguishable; must survive broad handlers\n\nclass RunBudgetController:\n    def __init__(self, call_cap: int): ...\n    def reserve(self) -> Reservation:          # atomic; raises RunBudgetExhausted if no slot\n    # Reservation is single-use; consumed on dispatch issue, even if the attempt fails\n    def audit(self) -> BudgetAudit: ...        # counts, cap, denials for safe metadata\n```\n`Reservation` authorizes **exactly one** dispatch attempt and cannot be reused. A denied `reserve()` dispatches nothing.\n\n### 15.3 State machine and concurrency\n- States per slot: `AVAILABLE → RESERVED → CONSUMED`; a reservation that is never dispatched (defensive) returns to `AVAILABLE` only via explicit, audited release; a dispatched attempt moves to `CONSUMED` regardless of success.\n- **Concurrency:** `reserve()` is atomic under a single lock/condition per controller; with 1 slot remaining and N concurrent callers, exactly 1 grants and N-1 raise. No branch overshoot allowance is needed (each concurrent branch holds its own reservation). Default START branches = 4 analysts + Memory Log (derived from constructed plan, not a hard-coded constant; branch count irrelevant to the strict bound).\n- **SDK retries:** `max_retries=0` for the guaranteed-budget mode; every application retry takes a **fresh** reservation. If a client cannot disable hidden retries, that client is **rejected** in guaranteed-budget mode (not silently uncovered). Gateway-internal retries are outside the client-side guarantee (stated, not hidden).\n\n### 15.4 Exhaustion propagation (must survive broad handlers)\n- `RunBudgetExhausted` must **not** be swallowed by `agents/structured.py` free-text fallback, `memory/settlement.py` (`except Exception`), or the graph memory step. D must either re-raise it or consult an authoritative exhausted-state check, so a refused **required** attempt reaches finalization as `BUDGET`.\n- **Trigger:** exhaustion stops a run only when a **required further** attempt is refused. Reaching the cap after the last needed request does **not** force failure; a workflow within cap completes normally.\n- **In-flight:** already-issued requests are accounted for (consumed); their termination is awaited before publishing immutable final counts. No new wall-clock termination guarantee is introduced by COST-002.\n\n### 15.5 Result / config / report / manifest / scorer compatibility (needed with BUDGET)\n- **`StopReason`:** add `\"BUDGET\"` ⇒ six values. Every reader that enumerates `StopReason` (`result.py`, classifiers, report/manifest validators, scorer) must be updated together; an old reader must **fail closed** on the new value, not silently coerce.\n- **Classifier precedence:** budget refusal is recognized **before** generic `INTERNAL_ERROR`/model classification. **Persistence failure stays primary** if critical report/manifest publication also fails; the budget cause is a secondary recorded diagnostic.\n- **Result fields:** on `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`: `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`; safe audit names configured cap and counts.\n- **Config:** `CALL_CAP` recorded in `EffectiveConfig` (safe) and manifest; open default is a configuration decision, not a measured number.\n- **Report/manifest:** add `run_budget` summary (cap, attempts, reservations, denials) — no prompts/secrets. `schema_version` bump with forward-compatible readers.\n- **Observability (NFR-OBS-001 dependency):** the BUDGET run's log names the **limit hit** (calls here; tokens/time if separately adopted).\n\n### 15.6 Runtime policy row\nAdds catalog **R17** (see `runtime-policy-catalog.md`): trigger = required request refused by adopted budget → `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`, partial content preserved through normal publication, no final rating, `NOT_RUN`; safe diagnostic (budget kind, limit, counters, run/attempt id).\n\n### 15.7 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)\n| # | Input | Expected | Violating negative |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| B1 | within-cap workflow | COMPLETED, normal | INCOMPLETE fails |\n| B2 | CALL_CAP=8, 7 consumed, 4 workers (injected barrier) | exactly 1 grant, 3 denials | 2 grants fails |\n| B3 | required attempt after cap exhausted | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET, NOT_RUN, rating null | INTERNAL_ERROR or COMPLETED fails |\n| B4 | exhaustion inside structured fallback/memory | BUDGET not swallowed | fallback hides it fails |\n| B5 | concurrent runs | isolated budgets per run | shared counter leaks fails |\n| B6 | budget stop + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary, budget secondary | two/zero reasons fails |\n| B7 | any controlled attempt without reservation | none possible (audit pairs 1:1) | unpaired attempt fails |\nCONTRACTS_EOF\necho \"appended §15\"; wc -l docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md"

Run-wide request-budget boundary — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002` + `BUDGET` (PROPOSED; prioritized first handoff)\n\nStatus: **proposed implementation-ready design**, consolidating `docs/architecture/proposals/reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md` and the stop-reason reply. **Not implemented.** This is the **first recommended implementation handoff** (§16): most isolated, offline-testable, unblocks a Must (`COST-002`) plus RUN-001's `BUDGET`.\n\n### 15.1 Component and boundary\n| Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `RunBudgetController` | One per run; issues single-use reservations; enforces `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; exposes exhausted state | `tradingagents/runapi/budget.py` | B / D / C / E |\n\n- The controller lives at the **controlled application client boundary** (where the app issues model-request attempts), shared across quick/deep tiers, structured/plain paths, retries and in-run memory/reflection. It must **not** be a global counter across runs; it must be **separate from the frozen input snapshot** (`RunContext`).\n- `CALL_CAP` is a **configuration value** (test value 8; production default open, **not a measured value**).\n\n### 15.2 Interface (proposed signatures)\n```\nclass RunBudgetExhausted(Exception): ...     # distinguishable; must survive broad handlers\n\nclass RunBudgetController:\n    def __init__(self, call_cap: int): ...\n    def reserve(self) -> Reservation:          # atomic; raises RunBudgetExhausted if no slot\n    # Reservation is single-use; consumed on dispatch issue, even if the attempt fails\n    def audit(self) -> BudgetAudit: ...        # counts, cap, denials for safe metadata\n```\n`Reservation` authorizes **exactly one** dispatch attempt and cannot be reused. A denied `reserve()` dispatches nothing.\n\n### 15.3 State machine and concurrency\n- States per slot: `AVAILABLE → RESERVED → CONSUMED`; a reservation that is never dispatched (defensive) returns to `AVAILABLE` only via explicit, audited release; a dispatched attempt moves to `CONSUMED` regardless of success.\n- **Concurrency:** `reserve()` is atomic under a single lock/condition per controller; with 1 slot remaining and N concurrent callers, exactly 1 grants and N-1 raise. No branch overshoot allowance is needed (each concurrent branch holds its own reservation). Default START branches = 4 analysts + Memory Log (derived from constructed plan, not a hard-coded constant; branch count irrelevant to the strict bound).\n- **SDK retries:** `max_retries=0` for the guaranteed-budget mode; every application retry takes a **fresh** reservation. If a client cannot disable hidden retries, that client is **rejected** in guaranteed-budget mode (not silently uncovered). Gateway-internal retries are outside the client-side guarantee (stated, not hidden).\n\n### 15.4 Exhaustion propagation (must survive broad handlers)\n- `RunBudgetExhausted` must **not** be swallowed by `agents/structured.py` free-text fallback, `memory/settlement.py` (`except Exception`), or the graph memory step. D must either re-raise it or consult an authoritative exhausted-state check, so a refused **required** attempt reaches finalization as `BUDGET`.\n- **Trigger:** exhaustion stops a run only when a **required further** attempt is refused. Reaching the cap after the last needed request does **not** force failure; a workflow within cap completes normally.\n- **In-flight:** already-issued requests are accounted for (consumed); their termination is awaited before publishing immutable final counts. No new wall-clock termination guarantee is introduced by COST-002.\n\n### 15.5 Result / config / report / manifest / scorer compatibility (needed with BUDGET)\n- **`StopReason`:** add `\"BUDGET\"` ⇒ six values. Every reader that enumerates `StopReason` (`result.py`, classifiers, report/manifest validators, scorer) must be updated together; an old reader must **fail closed** on the new value, not silently coerce.\n- **Classifier precedence:** budget refusal is recognized **before** generic `INTERNAL_ERROR`/model classification. **Persistence failure stays primary** if critical report/manifest publication also fails; the budget cause is a secondary recorded diagnostic.\n- **Result fields:** on `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`: `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`; safe audit names configured cap and counts.\n- **Config:** `CALL_CAP` recorded in `EffectiveConfig` (safe) and manifest; open default is a configuration decision, not a measured number.\n- **Report/manifest:** add `run_budget` summary (cap, attempts, reservations, denials) — no prompts/secrets. `schema_version` bump with forward-compatible readers.\n- **Observability (NFR-OBS-001 dependency):** the BUDGET run's log names the **limit hit** (calls here; tokens/time if separately adopted).\n\n### 15.6 Runtime policy row\nAdds catalog **R17** (see `runtime-policy-catalog.md`): trigger = required request refused by adopted budget → `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`, partial content preserved through normal publication, no final rating, `NOT_RUN`; safe diagnostic (budget kind, limit, counters, run/attempt id).\n\n### 15.7 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)\n| # | Input | Expected | Violating negative |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| B1 | within-cap workflow | COMPLETED, normal | INCOMPLETE fails |\n| B2 | CALL_CAP=8, 7 consumed, 4 workers (injected barrier) | exactly 1 grant, 3 denials | 2 grants fails |\n| B3 | required attempt after cap exhausted | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET, NOT_RUN, rating null | INTERNAL_ERROR or COMPLETED fails |\n| B4 | exhaustion inside structured fallback/memory | BUDGET not swallowed | fallback hides it fails |\n| B5 | concurrent runs | isolated budgets per run | shared counter leaks fails |\n| B6 | budget stop + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary, budget secondary | two/zero reasons fails |\n| B7 | any controlled attempt without reservation | none possible (audit pairs 1:1) | unpaired attempt fails |\nCONTRACTS_EOF\necho \"appended §15\"; wc -l docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md",

      "content": "# ADR 002 — Extended result contract, output-check v2, evidence/coverage and run budget\n\n- Status: **Proposed (architecture draft 2026-11-24)**. A **genuine new design cycle** for the broader proposed requirements. It is **separate** from, and does not modify, the preserved C2 evaluation (C1/C2/C3) in [ADR 001](001-portfolio-aware-cli.md). Not implementation; not team adoption of A's registry; D implementation and C acceptance are pending.\n- Deciders: Member B (author), pending A (requirements meaning/scope), C (verification), D (implementation feasibility), E (governance/CI).\n- Scope: `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`, `REQ-TA-FR-001/005/006/007/008`, `REQ-TA-SEC-003`, `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`, `REQ-TA-RUN-001` (`BUDGET`), and associated `REQ-TA-INV-*`. Detailed contracts are in [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §13–§16.\n- Does not supersede ADR 001. The two coexist: C2's input-service/immutable-`RunContext`/shared-execution boundary is the base these extensions build on.\n\n> Estimates are labelled **ESTIMATE**. No measurement, approval or historical alternative is invented. The old C2 candidate evaluation is preserved unchanged.\n\n## Context\n\nThe 24 November requirements snapshot (`requirements.yaml`, `status: proposed_for_adoption`) proposes obligations beyond the implemented `SEL-TA-*` baseline: an R1–R8 deterministic output check with a **corrected** finding class, an evidence-ID registry and per-run coverage record, a run-wide single-use request-budget controller and a `BUDGET` stop reason. The as-built system implements only Q1–Q4, five stop reasons, and input provenance (see interface-contracts §12). This ADR records the **bounded design decisions** needed to make those obligations implementable and testable, without claiming they are adopted or built.\n\n## Decisions (bounded alternatives)\n\n### D1 — Corrected findings may coexist with `PASSED` (approved published target)\n- **Chosen (target):** `Finding.status ∈ {BLOCKING, CORRECTED}`; **any BLOCKING ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW`; CORRECTED-only ⇒ `PASSED`**; corrected values recorded (`original`/`corrected`). This is the approved published target.\n- **Alternative (unapproved requirements-change only):** keep blocking-only (as-built). Recorded as a deferral alternative that would require a requirements change; **not** the target. Tradeoff: loses the ability to auto-downgrade (e.g., R5 confidence) while still passing.\n- **Impact:** `Finding`/`CheckResult` types, report rendering, manifest `check_rules_version`, scorer readers — shipped together.\n\n### D2 — R3 ownership check is a deterministic blocking phrase check (target)\n- **Chosen (target):** R3 is a **blocking phrase/pattern check** over the delivered body against A's banned-ownership list; a match ⇒ BLOCKING.\n- **Alternative (requires A/C/team agreement):** contextual handling — flagged only when not grounded in supplied facts, permitting quoted/conditional uses. Not reliably deterministic; would be a semantic-rubric matter. Recorded as an alternative, **not** an advisory replacement.\n- **Impact:** checker rule + fixture list; no model call.\n\n### D3 — Run budget: shared single-use reservation controller\n- **Chosen:** one run-scoped controller; atomic `reserve()` issuing single-use reservations; `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; SDK `max_retries=0` (reject clients that can't); exhaustion survives broad handlers; persistence failure stays primary.\n- **Alternatives considered:** (a) reusable semaphore — rejects (bounds concurrency, not cumulative calls); (b) counter at high-level invocations with SDK retries on — rejects (cannot guarantee the bound); (c) branch-overshoot allowance — rejects (unnecessary under single-use reservations).\n- **Tradeoff:** strict cap can starve a parallel branch that loses the last slot (stops rather than degrades) — the price of a checkable guarantee.\n\n### D4 — Evidence/coverage as separate registries feeding R2/R7\n- **Chosen:** dedicated `EvidenceRegistry` (stable IDs, resolution) and `CoverageTracker` (12-channel record, `NOT_REQUESTED`), built from tool results, deterministic render; R2/R7 integrate **after** these contracts are agreed.\n- **Alternative:** embed coverage in the checker — rejects (server-side determinism and R7 equality need a record, not a derived glance).\n- **Dependency:** channel↔method map and the two router-bypass call sites to be confirmed by D/C.\n\n### D5 — Resume identity (decision presented separately; not decided here)\n- **Alternatives:** (a) fresh `run_id` per invocation (current INV-12, chosen baseline); (b) logical-run identity + attempt identities with isolated artifacts (D's call; requires revising INV-11/12 wording). **Not chosen here; not promised.** Interruption semantics (`INTERRUPTED`) stay; resume is a separate contract change.\n\n## Consequences\n- Positive: a concrete, testable target for the broader requirements; corrected findings enable auto-downgrade checks without failing; the budget bound is enforceable; evidence/coverage become deterministic.\n- Negative/limits: larger result/report/manifest/scorer surface (version gates required); R3 deterministic phrase check cannot judge context; R5 corrected-only `PASSED` requires every reader to understand `CORRECTED`; evidence registry is the largest implementation risk before the deadline.\n- Preserved: ADR 001 / C2 selection and rationale; Q2 trusted-provenance guard (kept separately from R2); as-built Q1–Q4 behaviour remains the current description until implementation.\n\n## Related\n- Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md)\n- [../interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §13–§16; [001-portfolio-aware-cli.md](001-portfolio-aware-cli.md); [../runtime-policy-catalog.md](../runtime-policy-catalog.md); [../invariants.md](../invariants.md); [../traceability-inputs-member-b.md](../traceability-inputs-member-b.md)\n"

A commit records submitted changes; it does **not** by itself prove who manually authored the code. C's **independent acceptance remains pending**. The points it enforces:\n   - **Correspondence:** per case, the trusted `(input_mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of, kind)` is derived from the authoritative case definitions (`score_gov004.py::expected_case_identity`) and compared to the manifest; tier-provider settings must match the fixed configuration (`_tier_providers_match_fixed`); case/config/provenance/result and hash checks bind each report to its record.\n   - **Counterfeit rejection:** conflicting mirror copies and bare authoritative metadata lines outside the header block are rejected (`_reject_counterfeit_metadata_outside_header`; canonical-record equality for durability mirrors).\n   - **Unsuccessful-attempt accounting:** `replay_store.claim_start` records an exclusive, durable STARTED before dispatch under a cross-process lock; an unresolved start stays a non-completed denominator entry and blocks ID reuse; the scorer reports all started/completed attempts and separates retries.\n - **Baseline/team change.** These are C's verification-tooling changes (R2/R3), refined with B's design/B-remediation probes. The application product code is not the evaluator; the ledger and scorer are verification governance.\n",

## AR24 01 — Budget slot recycling contradicts the cumulative bound

**Contract choice (chosen):** make successful **admission monotonic**. A reservation consumes a cumulative admission slot the moment it is **granted**; an unused grant may be **invalidated** (and audited) but **never refunds capacity**. This preserves `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`. (Recycling-to-AVAILABLE is dropped; an alternative recycling policy would be a *different counting contract* and a requirements decision — recorded as an unapproved alternative in ADR-002, not the target.)

**Affected sections:** §15.2 (types + protocol), §15.3 (state machine/counterexamples), §15.7 (scenarios), invariants INV-18, ADR-002 D3, traceability §5 (scenario refs).

**Concrete types/protocol to add:**
```
Reservation { id: str; controller_run_id: str; state: GRANTED|CONSUMED|INVALIDATED }
BudgetAudit {
  call_cap: int
  granted: int          # cumulative successful admissions (monotonic)
  dispatched: int       # CONSUMED count
  invalidated: int      # granted-but-unused, capacity NOT refunded
  denied: int
}
RunBudgetController(call_cap, run_id):
  reserve() -> Reservation        # atomic; increments granted; denies if granted >= call_cap
  dispatch(res)                   # GRANTED -> CONSUMED; must be issued before the request; rejects foreign/again
  invalidate(res)                 # GRANTED -> INVALIDATED; keeps cumulative count; never frees capacity
```
- **Single use / run ownership:** `dispatch()`/`invalidate()` reject a reservation whose `state != GRANTED` (reuse) or whose `controller_run_id != self.run_id` (wrong run / cross-run reuse). Both raise a typed `BudgetProtocolError` (distinct from `RunBudgetExhausted`).
- **Between grant and request issue:** if the dispatch never issues (e.g., exception before send), `invalidate()` is called and audited; `granted` stays consumed.
- **Counter meanings fixed:** `granted` = cumulative successful reservations; `dispatched` = attempts actually issued; `denied` = refused `reserve()`; bound proven by `dispatched <= granted <= call_cap`.

**Verification examples (add to §15.7):**
- B8 (cap 1): grant A, invalidate A, reserve B → **denied** (granted already 1). Violating negative: a recycle that lets B be granted fails (`granted=2 > call_cap=1`).
- B9: dispatch A twice → second raises `BudgetProtocolError` (reuse rejected).
- B10: pass run-1 reservation to run-2 controller → `BudgetProtocolError` (wrong run).
- B11: grant then exception before dispatch → `invalidate`; `granted` unchanged; a later `reserve` at cap is denied.

## AR24 02 — Guaranteed-budget adapter and permitted files incomplete

**Resolved seam (verified).** Metering point = the **chat-model dispatch methods** the agents actually call:
- LLMs are created once per run at `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:79-80` via `create_tier_client(config, "deep"|"quick").get_llm()` (factory `tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py:142`; `BaseLLMClient.get_llm` at `llm_clients/base_client.py:55`).
- Agents dispatch via `llm.invoke(...)` and `llm.with_structured_output(...).invoke(...)` (e.g. `agents/structured.py:89,118`; research/risk managers/trader/debators; `agents/analysts/turn.py:27,30`), and memory reflection via `Reflector` (`memory/reflection.py`), memory settlement calls (`memory/settlement.py:159-181`), and the graph memory step `_memory_step` (`graph/trading_graph.py:311-335`).

**Contract choice (chosen):** a **run-scoped metering decorator** wrapping the run's chat-model objects, installed where `get_llm()` results are stored (`trading_graph.py:79-80`) — i.e., the controller is attached to the two tier models so quick+deep, structured, plain, retries, fallback and reflection inherited from those objects are all metered. Each `invoke`/`with_structured_output().invoke` first calls `controller.reserve()` + `controller.dispatch(res)`; a denied reserve raises `RunBudgetExhausted` **before** the SDK call.
- **Application attempt vs hidden transport retries:** one metered dispatch = one attempt at the application boundary. **SDK automatic retries must be `max_retries=0`** for guaranteed-budget mode (the OpenAI-compatible path already forwards `max_retries`, `llm_clients/openai_client.py` `_CHAT_KWARGS` at line ~213). Provider/gateway-internal retries are **outside** the client-side guarantee (stated, not hidden). Clients that cannot disable hidden retries are **rejected** in this mode.
- **Broad-handler survival:** `RunBudgetExhausted` must be re-raised (or authoritative-exhausted check consulted) in `agents/structured.py` (`except Exception`, line ~99), `memory/settlement.py` (`except Exception`, ~159/173) and `_memory_step` (`except Exception`, ~330). Those three hook files therefore MUST be in the budget slice's permitted set.

**Exact proposed write set (replace the vague template categories):**
- New: `tradingagents/runapi/budget.py`; new test area `tests/member_b_remediation/` (or a named new dir, chosen in planning; must be named in the approved plan).
- Edit (product): `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` (metering install + memory hook budget-awareness), `tradingagents/agents/structured.py`, `tradingagents/memory/settlement.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/result.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py` (enforce `max_retries=0` in budget mode + reject unsupported clients).
- Edit (manifest/validators): the manifest writer is in `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py`; the result-schema validator is `tradingagents/runapi/result.py`. “OBS fields” = `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` (only if a log field is required).
- **Template 3 must consume the human-approved exact file list** produced at planning (AR24 05), not a category list, and include the named test directory.

**Affected sections:** §15.1, §15.4, §15.8 (new “adapter/adapter seam” subsection), Template 3 (permitted files → “paste approved exact set”), traceability §5.

**Verification examples:** B2 (barrier last-slot), plus B12: attempt issued with SDK retries enabled in budget mode → rejected at construction (config error), not silently uncovered; B13: `invoke` path and `with_structured_output().invoke` path each consume exactly one reservation (audit pairs 1:1).

## AR24 03 — Output-check invariants and correction ordering conflict

**Contract choices (chosen):**

**(a) Restrict the equivalence to completed, evaluated runs.** Replace the global `PASSED iff no BLOCKING` with: *For a completed run whose checker was evaluated:* `PASSED ⇔ findings contain no BLOCKING (CORRECTED allowed)` and `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ ≥1 BLOCKING`; *INCOMPLETE ⇒ `NOT_RUN`, findings `[]`* (checker not invoked). Explicit negative added: **incomplete + empty findings must remain `NOT_RUN`, never `PASSED`.**

**(b) Coherent single-pass correction pipeline (no second verdict).** Type the v2 checker/normalizer explicitly and make it the **sole** authority on the delivered body:
```
CheckInput  { trusted: SafeInputMetadata; provenance_fragment: str;
              rendered_body: str;                 # body rendered+redacted once (§6)
              body_model_fields: BodyFields;      # structured fields the body was rendered from (e.g. sentiment header)
              evidence: EvidenceView;             # for R2 resolution (from §13 registry)
              coverage: CoverageSet | None }      # for R6/R7 (from §13)
CheckVerdict { output_check; findings: Finding[];
               corrected_fields: BodyFields | None }  # authoritative corrected values if any CORRECTED applied
```
Pipeline (one pass, one verdict): render+redact body once (§6) → build `CheckInput` → `Checker.evaluate(input) -> CheckVerdict` → **if** `corrected_fields` present, the renderer **re-renders the delivered body from `corrected_fields`** deterministically and the checker re-evaluates **only** the coverage-independent structural rules (Q3/Q4/R7) on the re-rendered body to prove *checked == delivered*; no rule is re-scored for a second competing verdict, and the findings list is frozen from the first evaluation. Store `corrected_fields` in the run record/manifest so the delivered content is authoritative and auditable.
- **Coexistence:** corrections and blocking findings may both be present; blocking dominates the verdict (`NEEDS_REVIEW`), corrections are still applied and recorded.
- **Where corrected values live:** `CheckVerdict.corrected_fields` → manifest field `corrected_fields` (safe, non-secret) + finding `original/corrected`.

**(c) Applicability (sentiment not selected / fields absent / all sources unavailable).**
- R4–R6 apply **only when the Sentiment Analyst was selected AND a `SentimentReport` exists**. If sentiment not selected → R4–R6 are **not applicable** (no finding), never a failure.
- R5/R6 source availability is taken from the **coverage record** (§13), NOT from `SentimentReport` (which has **no source-status field** — verified). All sources unavailable ⇒ R6 requires `Neutral` band; R5 caps confidence at `low` (corrected).
- Market-only fixture: unrequested channels are `NOT_REQUESTED`; an intentionally-unselected analyst produces **no** report and **no** R4–R6 finding; distinguish “not selected” (→ not applicable) from “selected but missing output” (→ treated per §6.3/incomplete or REVIEW, not silently pass).

**Affected sections:** §14.2 (equivalence + negative), §14.3 (pipeline + corrected_fields), new §14.8 “CheckInput/CheckVerdict types & ordering”, §6.2 cross-reference, invariants INV-17/INV-19, ADR-002 D1, traceability scenarios.

**Verification examples (K set):** K3 (R5 corrected ⇒ PASSED + corrected_fields applied, delivered body equals re-render), K10 (incomplete + [] ⇒ NOT_RUN), K11 (sentiment not selected ⇒ no R4–R6 finding, market-only PASSED), K12 (all three sources unavailable + Bullish ⇒ R6 blocking; + high confidence ⇒ R5 corrected), K13 (blocking R3 + R5 corrected ⇒ NEEDS_REVIEW, correction still recorded).

## AR24 03 (revised) — single final verdict over the delivered body

**Pipeline (no premature freeze):** render+redact body once (§6) → build `CheckInput{trusted, provenance, body, body_fields, evidence, coverage}` → **normalize** (apply authorized corrections to `body_fields` and deterministically re-render the body) → **evaluate once on the re-rendered delivered body** → emit the **single** `CheckVerdict{output_check, findings[], corrected_fields}` that describes exactly that delivered body. Corrections are applied *before* the one evaluation, so the verdict always covers what is delivered; there is no first-verdict-then-recheck. `corrected_fields` is persisted so delivered == checked == recorded.

**Equivalence (completed, evaluated only):** `PASSED ⇔ no BLOCKING (CORRECTED allowed)`; `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ ≥1 BLOCKING`; `INCOMPLETE ⇒ NOT_RUN, []` (checker not invoked). Negative: incomplete + `[]` must stay `NOT_RUN`.

**Selected-but-missing sentiment output — one explicit outcome:** if the Sentiment Analyst **was selected** but produced no `SentimentReport` (structured and free-text both failed), the run is **`COMPLETED` + `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `R_MISSING_SENTIMENT` (BLOCKING)`, final rating still parsed**. It is **not** incomplete and **not** silently passed. (Distinct from “not selected” ⇒ R4–R6 not applicable.) R5/R6 availability comes from the **coverage record**, not `SentimentReport` (which has no source-status field).

**Verification:** K3 (corrected ⇒ PASSED, delivered==re-render), K10 (incomplete+[] ⇒ NOT_RUN), K14 (sentiment selected, no report ⇒ COMPLETED/NEEDS_REVIEW/R_MISSING_SENTIMENT), K11 (not selected ⇒ no R4–R6), K12 (all sources down + Bullish ⇒ R6 blocking; high conf ⇒ R5 corrected).

## AR24 04 (completed) — coverage channels ≠ vendor calls

**Distinction:** a **coverage channel** is a reportable availability unit; a **vendor call** is one method invocation. Many calls can feed one channel; a channel is `OK` only if its required calls succeeded.

**Proposed grouping (derived from real code; explicitly pending A's authoritative 12-row table).** Router methods (`router.py:97-150`): `get_stock_data, get_indicators` → **price/technical (core)**; `get_fundamentals, get_balance_sheet, get_cashflow, get_income_statement` → **fundamentals/filings**; `get_news, get_global_news` → **news**; `get_insider_transactions` → **insider**; `get_macro_indicators` → **macro**; `get_prediction_markets` → **prediction (live-only)**. Non-router direct sources: `stocktwits`, `reddit` (sentiment), `company_profile` (Yahoo, context), `market_snapshot` (Yahoo, tools).

**Concrete discrepancy surfaced:** requirement says “12 channels, channels 3 and 11 bypass”; code has **11 router methods + 4 direct sources**, so “two bypass” is an undercount and the 12-index scheme is unreconcilable without A's table. Proposed resolution: a **grouped coverage set** (price-core, technical, fundamentals, filings, news, global-news, insider, macro, prediction-live, social-stocktwits, social-reddit, profile/snapshot → **12 reportable units**) with per-unit **availability** aggregated from its vendor call(s). Do **not** invent numeric indices; label this mapping “proposed, A to confirm”. `NOT_REQUESTED` = no selected analyst required any call for that unit.

**Additional contracts completed:** `EvidenceRegistry.register(item)->evidence_id` (dedup by `(channel, source, ticker, observed_at|published_at, value_hash)`; timestamps as supplied; lookup raises `EvidenceResolutionError`); thread-safe single lock; IDs attached at the **data boundary before agents see text**; citation syntax `[ev:ID]`; renderer emits `source` + `DATE` beside it (satisfies FR-001 visible source/date, not resolution alone). `CoverageTracker` init all units `NOT_REQUESTED`; a requested-but-unfinished unit ends `UNAVAILABLE`/`NO_DATA`; mixed success/failure/fallback aggregates worst-wins; core unit never requested ⇒ `NOT_REQUESTED` (not a gap; core rule applies only when requested). `value_ref` resolves to a run-owned retained-payload store under the run artifact dir; fields don't depend on unspecified storage; ordinary-failure retention is best-effort, not promised across critical persistence failure.

## AR24 05 (completed) — against installed plan/fingerprint/receipt protocol

Templates 1–3 must follow the real gate, not chat checkboxes:
1. **Read-only planning** (unchanged).
2. **Authorized preparation** of one front-matter plan at `docs/verification/plans/<feature-id>.md` with required fields (`feature_id, requirements[], implementation_paths[], test_files[], cases[normal|boundary|error|security], pass_condition`) **plus** the proposed test files (named) committed together — before product implementation.
3. **Human review** of that plan+tests.
4. **Documented approval command** (`/test-approval` on the exact plan/test commit) producing the trusted workflow receipt; archived under `docs/verification/approvals/`; receipt is fingerprint-bound.
5. **Product implementation only after** approval; later test changes require the policy's **renewed/split-scope** procedure (**not** rewriting frozen tests).

Template 4 (verification) stays a **different person**; self-approval is labelled `self_review` and never becomes independent acceptance. Note: **any commit/PR/approval/archive execution needs the user's authorization** and is **not run** in this documentation task.

## AR24 06 (completed) — exact rollout matrix

| Mode | check_rules_version | stop reasons | finding kinds | Q2 | Reader rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Budget-only** (Slice C ships first) | `1` (unchanged legacy checks) | 6 incl. `BUDGET` | `BLOCKING` only | **on** | readers accept `BUDGET`; Q1–Q4 unchanged |

## Confirmation — budget wrapper metering integrity

The wrapper is installed on the two tier chat-model objects at `trading_graph.py:79-80`, so **every** dispatch path through those objects is metered exactly once: plain `invoke`, `with_structured_output(...).invoke`, and `bind_tools(...).invoke` (bind returns a runnable over the **same** metered object — `agents/analysts/turn.py:30`). No double charge: the controller is attached to the **model object**, not re-wrapped per call site; a bound runnable delegates to the same `invoke`, so it fires one reserve+dispatch. Memory reflection (`Reflector` on `quick_thinking_llm`) and settlement calls inherit the same metered object. Residual to verify by D: that `with_structured_output`/`bind_tools` return proxies that route back through the wrapper’s `invoke` (LangChain runnable `.with_*` returns bound runnables over the same underlying model) — **T** to be asserted by a test that counts reservations across all three paths (B13). SDK retries forced `max_retries=0`; hidden transport retries outside the guarantee.
