Output-check v2 and result contract — `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`, `FR-007/008`, `SEC-003`, `INV-001..008` (PROPOSED target, not implemented)\n \n Status: **proposed published target** for D/C. The as-built checker is Q1–Q4 with blocking-only findings (§12.2). This section defines the proposed target: **R1–R8** with a **corrected** finding class such that **corrected-only findings may coexist with `PASSED`** and **blocking findings produce `NEEDS_REVIEW`**. It **preserves the existing Q2 trusted-provenance guard unchanged**; A's evidence-ID **R2 is a separate rule** that depends on §13. Implementation order: §13 data contracts first, then R2/R7 integration (§16).\n \n > **Namespace discipline.** `R1–R8` here = output-check rules (`REQ-TA-ARCH-002`). Distinct from: catalog runtime triggers `R1..R17` (`runtime-policy-catalog.md`), checker codes `Q1–Q4` (as-built), and the semantic rubric `R1–R7` (C). Do not equate by number.\n \n ### 14.1 Rule set (target)\n | Rule | Check | Owner req | Kind | Depends |\n |---|---|---|---|---|\n | R1 | Final rating readable (not REVIEW) | RUN-001 | Blocking | — |\n | R2 | Every cited evidence ID resolves to exactly one record | FR-001 | Blocking | **§13 EvidenceRegistry** |\n | R3 | No banned ownership phrase (ownership-assertion check) | FR-007 | Blocking | — |\n | R4 | Sentiment score lies in its band's range (only when sentiment selected & report present) | FR-008 | Blocking | — (applicability: §14.3) |\n | R5 | Sentiment confidence within coverage cap (downgrade to `low`, record safely) | FR-008 | **Corrected** | §13 coverage (source availability) |\n | R6 | No sentiment direction (non-Neutral band) when no source `OK` (only when sentiment selected & report present) | FR-008 | Blocking | §13 coverage |\n | R7 | \"Data coverage\" section equals the CoverageRecord (incl. `NOT_REQUESTED`) | FR-005 | Blocking | **§13 CoverageSet** |\n | R8 | Disclaimer present; no prohibited guarantee phrase | SEC-003 | Blocking | — |\n \n - **Q2 is preserved separately.** The existing **Q2 trusted-provenance guard** (envelope provenance fragment equals explicit trusted `SafeInputMetadata`, §6.4) remains an independent, always-on check on the frozen input identity. It is **not** replaced or absorbed by R2. R2 concerns **cited evidence IDs**, a different subject (report citations vs input provenance). Both can co-exist; a run can fail Q2 (provenance mismatch) while passing R2, or vice-versa.\n \n ### 14.2 Finding and result types, and the single-verdict pipeline (target)\n ```\n Finding {\n   rule: \"Q2\" | \"R1\"..\"R8\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"   # Q2 retained; R* per table\n   status: \"BLOCKING\" | \"CORRECTED\"           # NEW: corrected class added\n   detail: str                                # redacted\n   original: str | null                       # for CORRECTED: pre-correction value (safe field)\n   corrected: str | null                      # for CORRECTED: post-correction value (safe field)\n }\n CheckResult {\n   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n   findings: Finding[]\n   corrected_fields: SafeCorrectionFields | null  # ONLY explicitly-safe fields (e.g. sentiment confidence enum), never body text\n }\n ```\n \n **Single final verdict over the exact delivered body (no freeze-before-recheck).** The verdict must describe precisely what is delivered, so evaluation happens **once, on the final body**:\n \n 1. Render the body once from `final_state` + `RunContext` (§6.1), producing `body_fields`.\n 2. **Normalize first:** apply authorized corrections to `body_fields` (e.g. R5 confidence) → corrected `body_fields`.\n 3. **Re-render** the delivered body deterministically from the corrected `body_fields`.\n 4. **Redact the final re-rendered body** (`redactor.scrub`) — redaction happens **before** evaluation and before delivery, so the checked bytes equal the delivered bytes.\n 5. **Evaluate once** on that final redacted body: `Checker.evaluate(CheckInput{trusted, provenance, redacted_body, body_fields, evidence, coverage}) → CheckVerdict`. The single `CheckVerdict` (`output_check`, `findings`, `corrected_fields`) is the authoritative verdict for the delivered document. No second, competing verdict is produced.\n 6. Persist only the **safe** correction fields (`corrected_fields` restricted to enumerations/flags such as sentiment confidence/band/score — never narrative or free text), plus findings.\n \n **Result mapping (target), scoped to a completed, evaluated run:**\n - Any **BLOCKING** finding ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n - **Only CORRECTED** findings (no blocking) ⇒ `PASSED` (corrections already reflected in the re-rendered delivered body). *(Approved R5 target; see §16.)*\n - No findings ⇒ `PASSED`.\n - Checker exception ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW` with single `CHECK_ERROR`.\n - `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `NOT_RUN`, findings `[]` (checker **not invoked**).\n \n **Cross-field invariants (target), completed-and-evaluated only:**\n - For a completed run whose checker was evaluated: `PASSED ⇔ findings contain no BLOCKING (CORRECTED allowed)`; `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ ≥1 BLOCKING` (CHECK_ERROR counts as blocking).\n - **`INCOMPLETE ⇒ NOT_RUN` with findings `[]`.** Explicit negative: **incomplete + empty findings must remain `NOT_RUN`, never `PASSED`.** The `PASSED ⇔ no BLOCKING` equivalence therefore **does not** apply to incomplete runs.\n+\n+### 14.2a Typed v2 checker/evidence contracts (target)\n+\n+These are the exact types the pipeline (§14.2) and rules (§14.1) consume/produce. All are proposed; D implements, C tests.\n+\n+```\n+BodyFields {                       # the structured fields the body was rendered from (trusted inputs to render)\n+  final_rating: \"Buy\"|\"Overweight\"|\"Hold\"|\"Underweight\"|\"Sell\"|\"REVIEW\"|null\n+  sentiment: SentimentFields | null        # null iff sentiment analyst not selected OR no report\n+}\n+SentimentFields {                  # present only when sentiment selected AND a SentimentReport exists\n+  overall_band: \"Bullish\"|\"Mildly Bullish\"|\"Neutral\"|\"Mixed\"|\"Mildly Bearish\"|\"Bearish\"\n+  overall_score: float             # 0.0–10.0 (schema-bounded)\n+  confidence: \"low\"|\"medium\"|\"high\"\n+}\n+\n+EvidenceView {                     # read-only projection of the §13 EvidenceRegistry for R2\n+  resolve(evidence_id) -> EvidenceRecord | None    # None ⇒ dangling\n+  ids: set[str]                                     # admitted IDs for this run\n+}\n+CoverageView {                     # read-only projection of §13 CoverageSet for R6/R7\n+  channel_code(channel) -> \"OK\"|\"UNAVAILABLE\"|\"NO_DATA\"|\"STALE\"|\"WITHHELD\"|\"NOT_REQUESTED\"\n+  sentiment_source_status() -> {\"stocktwits\":\"OK\"|...,\"reddit\":...}   # per-source availability for R5/R6\n+  rendered_section() -> str        # deterministic coverage section for R7 equality\n+  mandatory_core_ok() -> bool      # strict: every mandatory core channel == OK (any NOT_REQUESTED ⇒ False)\n+}\n+\n+CheckInput {\n+  trusted: SafeInputMetadata                 # Q2 authoritative expected values (unchanged)\n+  provenance_fragment: str                   # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text)\n+  redacted_body: str                         # final re-rendered + redacted body (checked == delivered)\n+  body_fields: BodyFields                    # post-normalization fields the body was rendered from\n+  evidence: EvidenceView                     # R2\n+  coverage: CoverageView | null              # R5/R6/R7; null only when coverage not available (then R7 blocks)\n+  check_rules_version: 2\n+}\n+\n+CheckVerdict {                     # the single authoritative verdict for the delivered document\n+  output_check: \"PASSED\"|\"NEEDS_REVIEW\"|\"NOT_RUN\"\n+  findings: Finding[]                        # per §14.2\n+  corrected_fields: SafeCorrectionFields | null\n+}\n+```\n+\n+**`SafeCorrectionFields` — exact safe R5 projection (only these keys are ever persisted/emitted):**\n+```\n+SafeCorrectionFields {\n+  sentiment_confidence: \"low\" | \"medium\" | \"high\" | null   # R5 correction target; the ONLY corrected value in v2\n+}\n+```\n+- **R5 correction is exactly:** `corrected_fields.sentiment_confidence = \"low\"` when coverage shows a sentiment source not `OK` and the model chose `\"medium\"|\"high\"`. Nothing else is corrected in v2; **no narrative text, no scores, no free text, no holdings** enter `SafeCorrectionFields`.\n+- `Finding{R5, CORRECTED}` carries `original`/`corrected` as **enum strings** (`\"high\"→\"low\"`), which are safe; the `detail` is redacted. The `Finding` fields never carry narrative.\n+- If a future correction to `overall_score`/`overall_band` is proposed, it must be added to `SafeCorrectionFields` only after A/C agreement that the value is safe to persist; the current target corrects **confidence only**.\n+\n+**Evidence/check type rules:** `EvidenceView`/`CoverageView` are **read-only projections** (the checker never mutates the registries); `CheckInput.check_rules_version` is fixed to `2` for this target (§16.7); a checker that cannot build `CoverageView` emits a **blocking R7** (coverage section unavailable) rather than `PASSED`.\n - `RunResult`/manifest authority unchanged: `PASSED` still certifies only R1–R8, not truth or suitability.\n \n ### 14.3 Corrected-finding handling (R5) and sentiment-output cases — concrete\n \n **R5 correction (when sentiment is selected and a `SentimentReport` exists).** When coverage shows a sentiment source not `OK` and confidence `> low`: set `corrected_fields.sentiment_confidence=\"low\"` and `Finding{R5, CORRECTED, original=<high>, corrected=\"low\"}`. The re-render (§14.2 step 3) writes `low` into the delivered header; the single verdict is `PASSED` unless another rule blocks. Corrections and blocking findings may coexist; blocking dominates the verdict while the correction is still applied and recorded.\n \n **Sentiment-output cases (explicit, distinct):**\n - **Sentiment Analyst not selected** → R4–R6 **not applicable**; no finding. (Market-only fixture must not fail for an absent `SentimentReport`.)\n - **Both generation paths fail** (structured call and free-text fallback both yield nothing usable) → the run is **`INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE` / `output_check=NOT_RUN`, no final rating, no findings** (classified by the finalizer as a model failure; the checker is not invoked). This matches `REQ-TA-NFR-001`.\n - **Usable free text without structured fields** (the analyst produced usable narrative but no `SentimentReport`) → this is a **separate case**; it is **not** assigned a new adopted finding rule here. It is surfaced as an **open policy question for A/C** (whether to treat as `REVIEW`/`NEEDS_REVIEW` or to attempt extraction). The design records the case explicitly rather than inventing a rule.\n - **All three sources unavailable** (selected, report present) → R6 requires `Neutral` band (blocking if not); R5 caps confidence at `low` (corrected). Availability comes from the **coverage record** (`SentimentReport` has no source-status field).\n \n-This is a **contract extension** shipped together: `Finding.status` gains `CORRECTED`, `CheckResult` gains `corrected_fields` (safe only), `CheckResult(PASSED)` no longer requires empty findings, and report/scorer render/interpret the new fields under the `check_rules_version` gate (§14.5, §16.6).\n+This is a **contract extension** shipped together: `Finding.status` gains `CORRECTED`, `CheckResult` gains `corrected_fields` (safe only), `CheckResult(PASSED)` no longer requires empty findings, and report/scorer render/interpret the new fields under the `check_rules_version` gate (§14.5, §16.7).\n \n ### 14.4 R3 ownership phrase check — target is a **blocking phrase check**\n R3 is retained as a **deterministic blocking phrase/pattern check** over the delivered body for the banned-ownership list (`your position`, `current position`, `maintain the position`, `add to your position`, `exit your position`, `your holdings`, `you own`; list owned by A). A match ⇒ BLOCKING finding. This is the **published target**.\n - **Alternative (requires A/C/team agreement, NOT the target):** contextual handling — assess ownership assertions only when not grounded in supplied facts and permit quoted/conditional uses. This cannot be implemented reliably as a deterministic classifier; it would become a semantic-rubric matter. It is recorded as an **alternative requiring agreement**, **not** an advisory replacement for R3.\n - Interaction with R5-style correction: R3 corrections are **not** auto-applied; ownership wording is a content change the model must make, so R3 is blocking-only.\n \n ### 14.5 Report / manifest / scorer compatibility\n - **Report:** envelope gains nothing secret; the re-rendered body shows corrected values; the findings list distinguishes blocking vs corrected with `original`/`corrected` where applicable.\n-- **Manifest:** add `check_rules_version` **separately from** the manifest/result `schema_version` (§16.6). Keep `findings` shape additive.\n+- **Manifest:** add `check_rules_version` **separately from** the manifest/result `schema_version` (§16.7). Keep `findings` shape additive.\n - **Scorer readers:** must accept `CORRECTED` and `corrected_fields`; a reader that only knows `BLOCKING` **fails closed** on an unknown `status`/version (never silently treats `CORRECTED` as non-blocking).\n-- **Schema/version policy:** see §16.6 (separate manifest/result schema version and check-rule version; explicit legacy path for schema-1 artifacts lacking `check_rules_version`; reject unknown/invalid new-format combinations).\n+- **Schema/version policy:** see §16.7 (separate manifest/result schema version and check-rule version; explicit legacy path for schema-1 artifacts lacking `check_rules_version`; reject unknown/invalid new-format combinations).\n - **Safe-only persistence:** manifest/report carry only `corrected_fields` (enumerations/flags), never narrative/free text; redaction precedes evaluation and delivery.\n \n ### 14.6 Incomplete / raise / block / correct decision table (target)\n | Situation | run_outcome | output_check | findings |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | All rules pass | COMPLETED | PASSED | [] |\n | Only R5 corrected | COMPLETED | PASSED | [R5 CORRECTED] |\n | Any blocking rule fails | COMPLETED | NEEDS_REVIEW | ≥1 BLOCKING |\n | Checker raises | COMPLETED | NEEDS_REVIEW | [CHECK_ERROR] |\n | **Both sentiment paths fail** | **INCOMPLETE (`MODEL_FAILURE`)** | **NOT_RUN** | **[]** (no rating) |\n | Engine incomplete (other) | INCOMPLETE | NOT_RUN | [] |\n \n ### 14.7 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)\n | # | Input | Expected | Violating negative |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | K1 | clean completed report | PASSED, [] | — |\n | K2 | one blocking rule each (R1,R2,R3,R4,R6,R7,R8) | NEEDS_REVIEW + matching finding | wrong rule id fails |\n | K3 | R5 corrected only | **PASSED** + R5 CORRECTED(original,corrected); delivered header shows `low`; `corrected_fields.sentiment_confidence==\"low\"` | treating corrected as blocking fails; losing original/corrected fails; delivered body not matching re-render fails |\n | K4 | model text says \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" while R3 fails | NEEDS_REVIEW (model claim ignored) | PASSED fails |\n | K5 | checker raises | NEEDS_REVIEW + CHECK_ERROR | PASSED fails |\n | K6 | incomplete run | NOT_RUN, [] | checker invoked fails |\n | K7 | Q2 provenance mismatch but R2 ids resolve | NEEDS_REVIEW via Q2 (R2 independent) | conflating Q2/R2 fails |\n | K8 | dangling cited ID, provenance correct | NEEDS_REVIEW via R2 | PASSED fails |\n | K9 | R3 banned phrase present | BLOCKING (target phrase check) | downgrading to corrected fails |\n | K10 | incomplete + empty findings | **NOT_RUN** (never PASSED) | PASSED fails |\n | K11 | market-only run (sentiment not selected) | PASSED; **no** R4–R6 finding | failing for absent SentimentReport fails |\n | K12 | all 3 sentiment sources unavailable, band Bullish, confidence high | R6 BLOCKING + R5 CORRECTED (confidence→low) | passing without R6 fails; missing correction fails |\n | K13 | blocking R3 + R5 corrected | NEEDS_REVIEW; correction still applied + recorded | dropping the correction fails |\n | K14 | **both sentiment paths fail** | **INCOMPLETE/MODEL_FAILURE/NOT_RUN, no rating** | COMPLETED or a rating fails |\n | K15 | usable free text, no structured fields | recorded as an **open policy case** (no invented finding rule); not silently PASSED or silently INCOMPLETE without a decision | inventing an adopted rule fails |\n | K16 | redaction-sensitive text in corrected body | delivered body redacted **before** evaluation; checked bytes == delivered bytes | unredacted delivery or check-before-redact fails |\n \n ---\n \n ## 15. Run-wide request-budget boundary — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002` + `BUDGET` (PROPOSED; prioritized first handoff)\n \n Status: **proposed implementation-ready design**, consolidating `docs/architecture/proposals/reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md` and the stop-reason reply. **Not implemented.** This is the **first recommended implementation handoff** (§16): most isolated, offline-testable, unblocks a Must (`COST-002`) plus RUN-001's `BUDGET`.\n \n ### 15.1 Component and boundary\n | Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | `RunBudgetController` | One per run; issues single-use reservations; enforces `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; exposes exhausted state | `tradingagents/runapi/budget.py` | B / D / C / E |\n \n - The controller lives at the **controlled application client boundary** (where the app issues model-request attempts), shared across quick/deep tiers, structured/plain paths, retries and in-run memory/reflection. It must **not** be a global counter across runs; it must be **separate from the frozen input snapshot** (`RunContext`).\n - `CALL_CAP` is a **configuration value** (test value 8; production default open, **not a measured value**).\n \n ### 15.2 Interface (proposed signatures)\n ```\n class RunBudgetExhausted(Exception): ...       # distinguishable; must survive broad handlers\n class BudgetProtocolError(Exception): ...      # reuse / wrong-run / invalid transition\n \n Reservation {                                   # single-use; owned by one run/controller\n   id: str\n   controller_run_id: str\n   state: \"GRANTED\" | \"CONSUMED\" | \"INVALIDATED\"\n }\n BudgetAudit {\n   call_cap: int\n   granted: int          # cumulative successful admissions (MONOTONIC; never refunded)\n   dispatched: int       # CONSUMED count (attempts actually issued)\n   invalidated: int      # granted-but-unused; capacity NOT refunded\n   denied: int\n }\n \n class RunBudgetController:\n     def __init__(self, call_cap: int, run_id: str): ...\n     def reserve(self) -> Reservation:      # atomic; increments granted; raises RunBudgetExhausted if granted >= call_cap\n     def dispatch(self, res: Reservation):  # GRANTED -> CONSUMED; must be called BEFORE the request issue\n     def invalidate(self, res: Reservation):# GRANTED -> INVALIDATED; keeps cumulative count; NEVER frees capacity\n     def audit(self) -> BudgetAudit: ...    # safe counts for manifest/event metadata\n ```\n `Reservation` authorizes **exactly one** dispatch attempt and cannot be reused. A denied `reserve()` dispatches nothing. `dispatch()`/`invalidate()` raise `BudgetProtocolError` if `res.state != \"GRANTED\"` (reuse) or `res.controller_run_id != run_id` (wrong run / cross-run reuse). Between grant and request issue: if the dispatch never issues (exception before send), `invalidate()` is called and audited; `granted` stays consumed.\n \n ### 15.3 State machine and cumulative bound\n - States per reservation: `GRANTED → CONSUMED` (dispatched) or `GRANTED → INVALIDATED` (granted but unused). **There is no return to available capacity.** The `granted` counter is **monotonic**, so `dispatched <= granted <= CALL_CAP` holds even if an unused grant is invalidated: invalidating never lets a second grant happen at a cap of 1.\n - **Alternative (NOT the target):** a recycling policy that returns an unused slot to capacity would require a **different counting contract** and is an **explicit requirements decision**; it is recorded as an unapproved alternative (ADR 002 D3), not implemented.\n - **Concurrency:** `reserve()` is atomic under a single lock/condition per controller; with 1 slot remaining and N concurrent callers, exactly 1 grants and N-1 raise. No branch overshoot allowance is needed (each concurrent branch holds its own reservation). Default START branches = 4 analysts + Memory Log (derived from constructed plan, not a hard-coded constant; branch count irrelevant to the strict bound).\n - **SDK retries:** `max_retries=0` for the guaranteed-budget mode; every application retry takes a **fresh** reservation. If a client cannot disable hidden retries, that client is **rejected** in guaranteed-budget mode (not silently uncovered). Gateway-internal retries are outside the client-side guarantee (stated, not hidden).\n \n ### 15.4a Metering exactly once across plain / tool-bound / structured dispatch\n The controller is attached to the run's **tier chat-model objects** created at `trading_graph.py:79-80` (`create_tier_client(config,\"deep\"|\"quick\").get_llm()`), so every dispatch through them is metered:\n - **Plain:** `llm.invoke(...)` → one `reserve()+dispatch()`.\n - **Tool-bound:** `llm.bind_tools(tools).invoke(...)` — the bound runnable delegates to the same underlying metered `invoke`; the controller is on the model object, **not** re-wrapped per call site, so exactly one reservation is consumed (no missed, no double charge).\n - **Structured:** `llm.with_structured_output(schema).invoke(...)` — likewise routes through the same metered `invoke`.\n - **Memory/reflection:** `Reflector` uses the same `quick_thinking_llm`; settlement and the graph `_memory_step` calls inherit the metered object.\n - **No double charge:** because metering lives on the shared model object, wrapping it once covers all bound/proxied runnables; a probe asserts a bound/structured call does not create a second reservation.\n - **Proposed probes (C inputs; not yet run):** P1 plain=1 reservation; P2 tool-bound=1; P3 structured=1; P4 no double-wrap ⇒ not 2 per call; P5 each reservation pairs with ≤1 dispatched attempt; P6 wrong-run/reuse rejected. **Do not claim the runtime guarantee until these pass.**\n \n \n ### 15.4 Exhaustion propagation (must survive broad handlers)\n - `RunBudgetExhausted` must **not** be swallowed by `agents/structured.py` free-text fallback, `memory/settlement.py` (`except Exception`), or the graph memory step. D must either re-raise it or consult an authoritative exhausted-state check, so a refused **required** attempt reaches finalization as `BUDGET`.\n - **Trigger:** exhaustion stops a run only when a **required further** attempt is refused. Reaching the cap after the last needed request does **not** force failure; a workflow within cap completes normally.\n - **In-flight:** already-issued requests are accounted for (consumed); their termination is awaited before publishing immutable final counts. No new wall-clock termination guarantee is introduced by COST-002.\n \n ### 15.5 Result / config / report / manifest / scorer compatibility (needed with BUDGET)\n - **`StopReason`:** add `\"BUDGET\"` ⇒ six values. Every reader that enumerates `StopReason` (`result.py`, classifiers, report/manifest validators, scorer) must be updated together; an old reader must **fail closed** on the new value, not silently coerce.\n - **Classifier precedence:** budget refusal is recognized **before** generic `INTERNAL_ERROR`/model classification. **Persistence failure stays primary** if critical report/manifest publication also fails; the budget cause is a secondary recorded diagnostic.\n - **Result fields:** on `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`: `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`; safe audit names configured cap and counts.\n - **Config:** `CALL_CAP` recorded in `EffectiveConfig` (safe) and manifest; open default is a configuration decision, not a measured number.\n-- **Report/manifest:** add `run_budget` summary (cap, granted, dispatched, invalidated, denied) — no prompts/secrets. **`schema_version` and `check_rules_version` are separate axes** (§16.6); budget-only ships as `schema_version=2, check_rules_version=1` (legacy Q1–Q4 preserved), not a vague \"v2\".\n+- **Report/manifest:** add `run_budget` summary (cap, granted, dispatched, invalidated, denied) — no prompts/secrets. **`schema_version` and `check_rules_version` are separate axes** (§16.7); budget-only ships as `schema_version=2, check_rules_version=1` (legacy Q1–Q4 preserved), not a vague \"v2\".\n - **Observability (NFR-OBS-001 dependency):** the BUDGET run's log names the **limit hit** (calls here; tokens/time if separately adopted).\n \n ### 15.6 Runtime policy row\n Adds catalog **R17** (see `runtime-policy-catalog.md`): trigger = required request refused by adopted budget → `INCOMPLETE/BUDGET`, partial content preserved through normal publication, no final rating, `NOT_RUN`;         "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n@@ -1,272 +1,277 @@\n # Staged implementation prompt pack (Member B) — UNEXECUTED TEMPLATES\n \n Status: **unexecuted templates, 2026-11-24.** These are drafting artifacts for a *future* implementation handoff. **Architecture approval does not authorize code implementation.** Each slice's execution plan and test criteria still require prior human approval before any build, and the model-provider access constraint is stated below. No template here has been run; no code, tests, approvals or results are claimed.\n \n Scope of these templates: the prioritised slices in [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §13–§16 and [ADR 002](../adr/002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md):\n - **Slice C — run budget controller + `BUDGET`** (first handoff; §15).\n - **Slice A — evidence & coverage** (§13).\n - **Slice B — output-check v2 R1–R8** (§14).\n \n **Model access constraint (access, not a mandate).** As of drafting, DeepSeek V4 Flash is the only model available to Member B's OpenCode work via the school API key. This is an access constraint for this implementation route; it is **not** a course requirement, an evaluated model choice, or a restriction on TradingAgents' inherited provider capabilities. No model comparison or model-saving claim is made. **No credentials belong in any prompt or document**; provide keys only through the environment, never pasted into a prompt.\n \n **Baseline to cite in every prompt (verify before use):** repository `Le-kk/CS5351`; recorded local revision for this planning pack `a62b801a51e6310f3b46860f6d2790583a95e0e0` (or the then-current integration HEAD named by E). Read `requirements.yaml` (`schema_version 1.2.0`, `proposed_for_adoption`), `docs/req/selected-requirements.md`, the named architecture contracts, and `docs/reviews/project-integration-review-2026-11-24.md`.\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 1 — Read-only planning prompt\n \n Copy the block for the chosen slice. This stage **must not modify files**.\n \n ```\n You are planning (NOT implementing) a bounded change in the CS5351 TradingAgents\n repository. READ-ONLY: do not edit, create, delete, commit, push, pull, switch\n branches, reset or stash. Do not read .env, credentials, provider auth stores, or\n private raw transcripts. Do not run paid/live model tests.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n Baseline revision to inspect: <integration HEAD; planning pack used a62b801...>\n \n Read first:\n - requirements.yaml (schema_version 1.2.0, status proposed_for_adoption) — note\n   <REQ-TA-... IDs for this slice>; treat status/priority as A owns meaning.\n - docs/req/selected-requirements.md (implemented baseline scope).\n - docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md §<13|14|15> and §16.\n - docs/architecture/adr/002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md.\n - docs/architecture/invariants.md, runtime-policy-catalog.md (namespaces!).\n - The REAL source seams for this slice:\n     C_budget: tradingagents/runapi/{result.py,finalize.py,execution.py},\n       agents/structured.py, memory/settlement.py, graph memory step,\n       llm_clients/factory.py, runapi/reporting.py, report/manifest validators.\n     A_evidence_coverage: tradingagents/dataflows/router.py (+ the two router\n       bypass call sites), runapi/{persist.py,execution.py}.\n     B_checker_v2: tradingagents/runapi/{checks.py,result.py,reporting.py},\n       agents/schemas.py (SentimentReport); tests/member_c_verification/... for seam style.\n \n Produce a PLAN ONLY:\n 1. Component/module boundary and exact proposed file paths (new vs edited).\n 2. Interface signatures + field-level contracts (nullability + authority).\n 3. Normal sequence and state transitions.\n 4. Failure, concurrency, retry, privacy, persistence policies.\n 5. Compatibility/migration (schemas, readers, version gates).\n 6. Proposed verification scenarios: inputs, expected outputs/counters, and >=1\n    violating negative per behaviour. Label them PROPOSED C inputs; do not claim\n    accepted test IDs or results.\n 7. Dependency order and the first handoff.\n 8. Open decisions and feasibility limits (label ESTIMATE).\n \n Do not propose changes outside this slice. Do not adopt requirements, declare\n gates enforced, or claim test results. End by listing every file you would touch.\n You may inspect code/tests read-only; do not run the suite or live tests.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 2 — Human checkpoint via the installed approval protocol\n \n This is a **human gate** that uses the **repository's actual test-approval protocol**, not a chat checkbox. It has two sub-stages: (2a) prepare plan + proposed tests, then (2b) approve them through the trusted workflow. A filled chat block is **not** the workflow receipt the checker verifies.\n \n ```\n 2a — AUTHORIZED PREPARATION (before product implementation)\n Produce, on a branch/commit (execution still requires your authorization; do not\n run during a documentation task):\n - One front-matter plan at  docs/verification/plans/<feature-id>.md  with the\n   REQUIRED fields read by scripts/ci/check_test_approval.py:\n     feature_id, requirements[], implementation_paths[], test_files[], cases[],\n     pass_condition\n   Cases must include at least one each of kind: normal | boundary | error | security,\n   each with an explicit expected result.\n - The NAMED test files listed in test_files[] (proposed tests), committed in the\n   SAME commit as the plan. Their file fingerprints are what the receipt binds.\n - implementation_paths[] = the exact approved write set (no vague categories).\n Reviewer reads the plan + proposed tests and records adequacy, incl. negatives.\n \n 2b — APPROVAL THROUGH THE TRUSTED WORKFLOW (not chat)\n-- The explicitly authorized reviewer posts, on the exact plan/test commit, the\n-  EXACT comment command:   /approve-tests <FULL 40-CHARACTER COMMIT SHA>\n-  (the command must match exactly; a short SHA, extra text or edited comment is\n-  rejected by the trusted workflow.)\n+- The authorized reviewer posts the EXACT comment command **on the OPEN FEATURE PR**\n+  (its `issue_comment`; the workflow requires `github.event.issue.pull_request`):\n+      /approve-tests <FULL 40-CHARACTER COMMIT SHA>\n+  The comment must match exactly (a short SHA, extra text or an edited comment is\n+  rejected). The SHA names the plan+test commit on that PR.\n - The trusted workflow (test-approval.yml -> test-approval-complete.yml) produces\n-  a RECEIPT bound to the comment text, the approved commit and the test-file\n+  a RECEIPT bound to the comment, the approved commit and the test-file\n   fingerprints. Archive the accepted record under docs/verification/approvals/.\n - Product implementation starts ONLY after a successful receipt for that commit.\n-- If tests change after approval, the policy's RENEWED / SPLIT-SCOPE procedure\n-  applies: re-approve the new test commit; do not silently rewrite frozen tests\n-  (later changed fingerprints are rejected).\n+- **Approved test files are FROZEN during product implementation.** Do not edit\n+  them to make implementation pass; changed test fingerprints are rejected. If a\n+  test must change, use the policy's RENEWED / SPLIT-SCOPE procedure (re-approve\n+  the new test commit) — never silently rewrite frozen tests.\n - Revocation uses /revoke-tests (a revocation receipt stays in force).\n - Self-approval is permitted but is labelled `self_review`; it is NOT independent\n   human acceptance. Retain actual reviewer attribution.\n \n Reviewer confirmations (recorded, not backdated):\n 1. Scope bounded; no edits to canonical requirements, other members' tests/CI/\n    evidence, or files outside implementation_paths[].\n 2. Test criteria adequate BEFORE implementation; a failing/violating test defined\n    before product code.\n 3. Result-contract/compat + version-gate plan acceptable.\n 4. Provider/model access constraint acknowledged; no credentials in any file.\n 5. One-slice approval does not approve other slices.\n \n Receipt reference to record:  approval_id: ______  approved_commit (40): ______\n NOTE: This gate approves PLAN + TESTS via the pinned receipt. It does not adopt\n requirements or certify verification. Any commit/PR/approval/archive action needs\n explicit authorization when executed and is not performed in a documentation task.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 3 — Build prompt (only after a successful Template 2 receipt)\n \n ```\n You are implementing an APPROVED, bounded slice in CS5351 TradingAgents.\n Proceed ONLY if a successful test-approval RECEIPT exists for this exact commit\n-(recorded via the trusted workflow; comment `/approve-tests <FULL 40-CHAR SHA>`\n-on the plan+test commit, archived under docs/verification/approvals/). If the\n-receipt is absent, for a different commit, or the test-file fingerprints differ,\n-STOP — do not implement.\n+(recorded via the trusted workflow; the reviewer posts `/approve-tests <FULL\n+40-CHAR SHA>` on the OPEN FEATURE PR, receipt archived under\n+docs/verification/approvals/). If the receipt is absent, for a different commit,\n+or the test-file fingerprints differ, STOP — do not implement.\n+APPROVED TEST FILES ARE FROZEN: do not edit them during implementation; a needed\n+test change uses the renewed/split-scope procedure (re-approve), never a silent\n+rewrite.\n Do not expand scope. Do not edit files outside the APPROVED implementation_paths[]\n from the plan. Do not touch canonical requirements, other members' tests/CI/\n evidence, or secrets. Work offline with the scripted/offline profile; no paid/live.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n Approval receipt: approval_id ______  approved_commit (40) ______\n \n PERMITTED FILES = the EXACT implementation_paths[] from the approved plan plus the\n approved test_files[]. Do not use category names. The approved set must explicitly\n include every mandatory hook for the slice; if it does not, STOP and escalate\n (Template 5) rather than editing an unapproved file. Authoritative examples the\n plan must have covered (exact repo-relative paths):\n   C_budget (metering + budget): new tradingagents/runapi/budget.py;\n     tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py (attach controller to deep/quick llm at\n     :79-80; budget-aware _memory_step); tradingagents/agents/structured.py\n     (re-raise budget); tradingagents/memory/settlement.py (re-raise budget);\n     tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py (force max_retries=0 in budget mode,\n     reject unsupported clients); tradingagents/runapi/result.py, finalize.py,\n     execution.py, reporting.py, persist.py (manifest), events.py (log fields).\n   A_evidence_coverage: new tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py, coverage.py;\n     tradingagents/dataflows/router.py; the direct-source call sites\n     tradingagents/agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py,\n     tradingagents/agents/context.py, tradingagents/agents/tools.py;\n     tradingagents/runapi/persist.py, execution.py.\n   B_checker_v2: tradingagents/runapi/checks.py, result.py, reporting.py;\n     tradingagents/agents/schemas.py (only if a field is required); manifest field\n     additions (separate schema_version vs check_rules_version).\n TESTS: named in the approved plan test_files[]; do not modify existing C-owned\n     tests unless the plan explicitly lists them (otherwise renewed/split-scope).\n \n MET/POINTS (budget): reserve() single-use atomic; dispatch() pairs GRANTED->CONSUMED;\n   invalidation never refunds cumulative admission (monotonic granted<=CALL_CAP);\n   wrap the run's deep/quick chat models so plain invoke, bind_tools(...).invoke and\n   with_structured_output(...).invoke each consume EXACTLY ONE reservation (no missed\n   or double charge); RunBudgetExhausted survives structured/settlement/memory broad\n   handlers; budget recognized BEFORE generic classification; PERSISTENCE_ERROR stays\n   primary over BUDGET. Do NOT claim a runtime metering guarantee before the\n   verification probes (B-variants) pass.\n \n ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (must hold; mirror the approved test list):\n   <paste the approved proposed scenarios for the slice (e.g. B1-B7 / E1-E12 / K1-K16)>\n   Each criterion needs a passing positive and at least one violating negative.\n   For the budget slice these MUST include the metering probes:\n     - plain llm.invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - llm.bind_tools(...).invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - llm.with_structured_output(...).invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - a path that would double-wrap/double-count is rejected by the probe\n     - structured/settlement/memory broad handlers do not swallow RunBudgetExhausted\n     - invalidate/reserve/re-reserve at cap is denied (monotonic admission)\n     - wrong-run / reuse of a reservation is rejected (BudgetProtocolError)\n \n SCOPE LIMITS:\n - No change to public engine signatures beyond what the slice requires; preserve\n   upstream tests where unaffected.\n - No new provider/model, no credentials, no live tests, no network.\n - Do not mark requirements satisfied, do not claim verification, do not adopt scope.\n - If a genuine ambiguity affects correctness, STOP and ask (see Template 5).\n \n DELIVERABLES: code + regression tests + a short note of exact commands run\n (offline) and their outcomes captured in the interaction. Do not commit/push.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 4 — Verification prompt (checks, outcomes, negatives, evidence)\n \n ```\n You are verifying an implemented, approved slice in CS5351. You are NOT the\n implementer. Verify against the approved plan and acceptance criteria. Do not\n modify application code or the implementation's tests to make them pass.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n Approved plan/acceptance revision/hash: <from Template 2/3>\n \n CHECKS TO RUN (offline; scripted model; record exact commands + results):\n - Targeted slice tests, then the prior offline suite, Ruff, dependency and\n   whitespace checks. Use the project virtual environment; no paid/live calls.\n - Positive cases: each approved scenario passes.\n - NEGATIVE cases (must fail as designed):\n     C_budget: >CALL_CAP attempts admitted; exhaustion swallowed by fallback;\n       shared counter across runs; budget relabelled INTERNAL_ERROR; BUDGET stop\n       overriding a co-occurring persistence failure.\n     A_evidence_coverage: dangling cited ID passes; unrequested channel mislabelled\n       as gap; core-gap completes; coverage section differs under prose change.\n     B_checker_v2: CORRECTED treated as NEEDS_REVIEW; BLOCKING treated as PASSED;\n       Q2 and R2 conflated; R3 phrase downgraded to corrected; model \"PASSED\" text\n       overriding a blocking rule.\n - Compatibility: a reader that enumerates old StopReason / old finding status\n   fails closed on the new value (not silent coercion); schema_version behavior.\n \n EXPECTED OUTCOMES: state precisely per case (counters, fields, status, stop_reason,\n output_check, paths null/not-null). Compare to the approved criteria; do not relax.\n \n EVIDENCE TO RETAIN: the exact commands, stdout/exit codes, the new/changed test\n files (paths), and any captured manifests/events for the positive and negative\n runs. Do not overwrite existing retained evidence; write to a new path if live is\n ever used (it is not in this template). Distinguish test DEFINITION, developer\n diagnostic and independent acceptance.\n \n VERDICT: report PASS/FAIL/PENDING per criterion with the evidence path. This is a\n verification recommendation; independent acceptance remains C's recorded decision.\n Do not claim team adoption or requirement satisfaction.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 5 — Review and escalation conditions\n \n ```\n STOP AND ESCALATE (to the human approver / B / C) if any of the following occurs;\n do not silently work around it:\n \n 1. A required change falls OUTSIDE the permitted file set (Template 3).\n 2. A genuine ambiguity or conflicting contract affects correctness (e.g. channel\n    map or bypass indices unknown; whether BUDGET is retained; R5/R3 scope unresolved;\n    resume identity). Surface it; do not decide A/C/team scope.\n 3. A negative test cannot be made to fail as designed (criterion unmet).\n 4. The result-contract/compat change would break an existing reader without a\n    version gate; propose the gate, do not weaken validation.\n 5. A failure would tempt relabelling a stop reason, hiding an attempt, skipping a\n    gate, or editing retained evidence to go green.\n 6. Any request to edit canonical requirements, other members' files/tests/CI/\n    evidence, or to run paid/live tests.\n 7. Provider/model access: if the only available model for this route cannot satisfy\n    the offline/scripted requirement or would require credentials in a file, stop.\n \n REVIEW EXPECTATIONS:\n - Implementer and verifier are different people where practical.\n - The verifier reproduces original negatives with black-box/synthetic probes, not\n   only the implementer's new tests.\n - All chronology (plan approval -> tests -> implementation -> verification) is\n   recorded in the authentic interaction; nothing is backdated.\n - Historical F8 stays unverified; current acceptance is a separate result.\n \n On escalation: state the concrete choice, the options, the impact and the exact\n minimum approval needed. Do not proceed past the approved scope without it.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template usage notes (human, not agent)\n \n - Run per slice; do not bundle all three into one unapproved mega-change.\n - **First handoff = Slice C (budget + BUDGET)** (interface-contracts §16.1): most isolated, offline-testable, unblocks a Must plus `BUDGET`.\n - **Evidence/coverage data contracts (Slice A §13) must be agreed before** Slice B's R2/R7 checker integration (approved dependency order).\n - These are **unexecuted templates**: no build, test, approval or result has occurred. Each single in a new interaction, with the **pinned approval protocol** between Template 2 and Template 3 (front-matter plan + named tests committed, then `/approve-tests <full 40-char SHA>` receipt).\n - **Do not claim a runtime metering guarantee** (or any \"exactly once\" property) before the verification probes pass; before that, ≤1-attempt intent and the tests are the only evidence.\n - Preserve authentic interactions for D5; do not backdate approvals; a handoff summary is not a raw transcript.\n",

Maps each supported failure/degraded path to trigger, responsible component, fallback/action, output and diagnostic/monitor, consistent with the selected result/check contract (`SEL-TA-FR-007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001`). Components exist in the `a62b801` checkout (verified); test evidence is C's; enforcement wiring is D/E's. No measured results are claimed.\n \n > **Label namespace warning:** the `R1`, `R2`, … in the **first column of the table below are trigger-row identifiers in this catalog only**. They are **not** the output-check rules `R1–R8` of proposed `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`, and **not** the checker codes `Q1–Q4` in `runapi/checks.py`. For example, catalog `R1` here is a recoverable-data sentinel path, whereas `REQ-TA-ARCH-002`'s `R1` is \"final rating readable\". Do not equate them by number.\n \n ## Result contract reminder\n - `run_outcome = COMPLETED | INCOMPLETE`.\n - `COMPLETED`: graph returned; final `rating ∈ {Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, REVIEW}`.\n - `INCOMPLETE`: no final rating; `stop_reason ∈ {MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED}`.\n - `output_check = PASSED | NEEDS_REVIEW | NOT_RUN`; incomplete ⇒ NOT_RUN.\n - Progress vocabulary (events) is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n \n | # | Trigger | Responsible component | Fallback / action | Output | Diagnostic / monitor |\n |---|---|---|---|---|---|\n | R1 | Recoverable non-core data unavailable (upstream sentinel) | Engine/tools (baseline behaviour preserved) | Continue run with the sentinel/absent marker; **do not** classify fatal | COMPLETED (or normal) | Event notes degraded node; **not** an incomplete reason |\n | R2 | Structured-output invocation fails, free text usable | `structured.py` path → PM text fallback | Use free-text; parse rating deterministically; the warning's exception detail is passed through the shared `Redactor` before logging (R1) | COMPLETED; rating if readable else REVIEW | Existing structured-fallback warning retained, redacted |\n | R3 | Model/provider output exhausted | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; no final rating | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE` | `event=run.terminal`; redacted cause |\n | R4 | Raised vendor/data exception (unrecovered) | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; typed result | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=DATA_FAILURE` | Redacted data exception message |\n | R5 | Ordinary internal exception | `runapi/finalize.py` | Stop; typed result, no escape past public entry | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` | Redacted traceback summary |\n | R6 | Malformed/invalid portfolio input | `runapi/input_service.py` (precheck + upstream model) | Stop **before dispatch**; filename + bad field/path, no contents/credentials | No run (pre-run rejection) | Input diagnostic; zero LLM calls |\n | R7 | As-of mismatch (`--portfolio-as-of` ≠ analysis date) | `runapi/input_service.py` | Stop before dispatch | Pre-run input error | Field-level diagnostic |\n | R8 | Selected file changed after confirmation | (no reread) | **Ignore** changed bytes; use frozen snapshot | Normal run with frozen identity | (no silent change; provenance records frozen digest) |\n | R9 | Output check rule broken (Q1–Q4) | `runapi/checks.py` | Do not pass; mark review needed | If graph returned: COMPLETED + NEEDS_REVIEW + blocking finding(s) | `event=output.check` findings |\n | R10 | Checker raises exception | `runapi/checks.py` (fail closed) | Blocking `CHECK_ERROR` | COMPLETED retained if graph returned, but NEEDS_REVIEW | `event=output.check` `CHECK_ERROR` |\n | R11 | Model text claims \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" but a rule fails | `runapi/checks.py` authority | Model claim ignored | NEEDS_REVIEW | Authority-source tag on check event |\n | R12 | Cooperative cancellation | `runapi/execution` + CLI coordinator | Stop cooperatively (if during run) or zero-start (pre-run) | Pre-run: no completed run; during run: INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERRUPTED` | `event=input.consent`/`run.terminal` |\n | R13a | Critical report/manifest staging or commit failure before rename (terminal-event append excluded) | `runapi/persist.py` + `runapi/finalize.py` | No rename; nothing visible at published path; revise logical outcome | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null` | Redacted persistence diagnostic; `_staging` not treated as published | \n | R13b | Best-effort sink failure (state JSON or message log) | `runapi/persist.py` | Continue; redacted note; does not flip a completed decision | Normal outcome unchanged | Redacted note | \n | R14 | Terminal-event JSONL append to staging fails (best-effort, non-critical) | `runapi/events.py` | Commit still publishes; logical outcome preserved (not PERSISTENCE_ERROR); manifest states non-durable terminal | Normal logical outcome; `terminal_event.durable=false` in manifest | Redacted diagnostic; later progress append never changes manifest | \n | R13c | Critical report/manifest staging/commit failure (R13a) after a tentative terminal was staged (R5) | `runapi/events.py` + `runapi/persist.py` + `runapi/execution.py` | Discard the stage-private tentative terminal; never expose a caller-visible COMPLETED; emit exactly one INCOMPLETE terminal matching the returned result | INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR/NOT_RUN; single INCOMPLETE terminal in caller sink | Redacted persistence diagnostic; no stale COMPLETED |\n | R15 | Workflow returns unreadable final text | `runapi/finalize.py` + `runapi/checks.py` | Complete with REVIEW | COMPLETED + rating REVIEW + NEEDS_REVIEW | Q1 finding |\n | R16 | Same-ticker/date second fresh run | `runapi/persist.py` / coordinator (run-ID isolation) | Write to a **new** run dir; refuse overwrite of prior artifacts | New isolated artifacts; first run unchanged | `event=output.persist` |\n \n ## Ordering and conditions\n - Every incomplete result has `output_check=NOT_RUN`; every completed result has a rating (REVIEW allowed) and a check result.\n - `MODEL_FAILURE` is used **only** for exhausted model/provider output failures; recoverable optional-data sentinels (R1) are never reclassified as fatal.\n - Diagnostics are redacted (NFR-003) before delivery; secrets/holdings never appear.\n - Durability across total disk failure/power loss is **not** promised; PERSISTENCE_ERROR is the cooperative failure contract.\n \n ## As-built status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n Rows R3–R5 (`MODEL_FAILURE`/`DATA_FAILURE`/`INTERNAL_ERROR`) and R12 (`INTERRUPTED`) map to `runapi/finalize.py::classify_exception`; R13a/R13c/R14 map to `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename`, truthful `terminal_event.durable`) and `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal). R9–R11, R15 map to `runapi/checks.py` (`Q1–Q4`, `CHECK_ERROR`). The vocabulary is **five** stop reasons; there is **no `BUDGET` row** implemented. Proposed budget rows (`REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002`/`COST-001/002` → `BUDGET`) are **not** in this catalog as implemented behaviour; they would require a sixth `stop_reason` and every reader updated.\n \n ## Proposed rows for the extended checks (2026-11-24; **PROPOSED, not implemented**)\n \n These are **catalog triggers** (the `R*` prefix here is the catalog namespace, **not** ARCH-002 rules or Q1–Q4). They accompany interface-contracts §13–§15 and ADR 002.\n \n | # | Trigger | Responsible component | Fallback / action | Output | Diagnostic / monitor |\n |---|---|---|---|---|---|\n | R17 | A **required** model request is refused by an adopted run budget (`CALL_CAP`) | `runapi/budget.py` → shared execution boundary → finalizer | Refuse the request; no prompts/secrets |\n-| R18 | Core data channel has code ≠ `OK` (price `UNAVAILABLE`/`NO_DATA`/`STALE`) | `runapi/coverage.py` + finalizer | Stop as data failure; do not publish a successful analysis | `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=DATA_FAILURE`, `NOT_RUN` | Channel + code; source metadata |\n+| R18 | **Mandatory core** data channel has code ≠ `OK` — including `NOT_REQUESTED` when the core channel was mandated but never requested (price `UNAVAILABLE`/`NO_DATA`/`STALE`/`NOT_REQUESTED`) | `runapi/coverage.py` + finalizer | Stop as data failure; do not publish a successful analysis. **Strict published rule:** an unrequested mandatory core channel is NOT auto-exempt; excluding it requires an adopted A/team exemption (not applied) | `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=DATA_FAILURE`, `NOT_RUN` | Channel + code; source metadata |\n | R19 | Non-core channel gap / statement `STALE` | `runapi/coverage.py` | Continue; code the channel; show `STALE` with filing date | `COMPLETED` (or normal) | Coverage section reflects code |\n | R20 | Output check produces **corrected only** finding (e.g. R5 confidence) | `runapi/checks.py` | Apply correction; record original+corrected | `COMPLETED` + `PASSED` + CORRECTED finding | `output.check` corrected finding |\n | R21 | Output check blocking rule fails (R1–R4,R6–R8) or checker raises | `runapi/checks.py` | Do not pass; retain findings | `COMPLETED` + `NEEDS_REVIEW` | Blocking finding / `CHECK_ERROR` |\n \n **Precedence:** if a budget stop (R17) and a critical persistence failure co-occur, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is primary and the budget cause is secondary (R13a unchanged). Reaching `CALL_CAP` after the last needed request does not itself trigger R17.\n",

All are proposed; D implements, C tests.\n+\n+```\n+BodyFields {                       # the structured fields the body was rendered from (trusted inputs to render)\n+  final_rating: \"Buy\"|\"Overweight\"|\"Hold\"|\"Underweight\"|\"Sell\"|\"REVIEW\"|null\n+  sentiment: SentimentFields | null        # null iff sentiment analyst not selected OR no report\n+}\n+SentimentFields {                  # present only when sentiment selected AND a SentimentReport exists\n+  overall_band: \"Bullish\"|\"Mildly Bullish\"|\"Neutral\"|\"Mixed\"|\"Mildly Bearish\"|\"Bearish\"\n+  overall_score: float             # 0.0–10.0 (schema-bounded)\n+  confidence: \"low\"|\"medium\"|\"high\"\n+}\n+\n+EvidenceView {                     # read-only projection of the §13 EvidenceRegistry for R2\n+  resolve(evidence_id) -> EvidenceRecord | None    # None ⇒ dangling\n+  ids: set[str]                                     # admitted IDs for this run\n+}\n+CoverageView {                     # read-only projection of §13 CoverageSet for R6/R7\n+  channel_code(channel) -> \"OK\"|\"UNAVAILABLE\"|\"NO_DATA\"|\"STALE\"|\"WITHHELD\"|\"NOT_REQUESTED\"\n+  sentiment_source_status() -> {\"stocktwits\":\"OK\"|...,\"reddit\":...}   # per-source availability for R5/R6\n+  rendered_section() -> str        # deterministic coverage section for R7 equality\n+  mandatory_core_ok() -> bool      # strict: every mandatory core channel == OK (any NOT_REQUESTED ⇒ False)\n+}\n+\n+CheckInput {\n+  trusted: SafeInputMetadata                 # Q2 authoritative expected values (unchanged)\n+  provenance_fragment: str                   # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text)\n+  redacted_body: str                         # final re-rendered + redacted body (checked == delivered)\n+  body_fields: BodyFields                    # post-normalization fields the body was rendered from\n+  evidence: EvidenceView                     # R2\n+  coverage: CoverageView | null              # R5/R6/R7;
